Overview

Join our Indoor GIS team as a Senior Software Developer and help shape the future of how people understand, navigate, and interact with the built environment. You will lead the development of advanced Indoor GIS capabilities that combine AI, computer vision, 3D reality capture, and spatial data to automate indoor mapping workflows and create innovative geospatial products from floor plans, 3D scans, and 360° imagery.

As a senior engineer, you will own complex features end-to-end, drive technical direction, mentor developers, and work across teams to turn emerging AI technologies into production-ready solutions. If you enjoy solving challenging problems and working with technologies like Large Language Models, computer vision, 3D graphics, and geospatial systems, this role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on the future of Indoor GIS.

Indoor GIS supports mission-critical operations for public safety agencies, helping police, fire, and emergency responders quickly understand complex buildings during emergency incidents. It also enables organizations such as airports, hospitals, campuses, and enterprises to optimize space utilization, manage occupants and visitors, and improve indoor navigation and wayfinding experiences.

Esri has a Relocation Assistance Program and can provide support with relocating to the Redlands, CA area for this position.

Responsibilities

  • Prototype, architect, and implement production-quality components for AI-assisted indoor mapping, feature extraction, indoor reality visualization, and geospatial data creation workflows
  • Lead technical exploration of Gaussian splats, 3D mesh-derived level generation, visual positioning, semantic search, and reality capture integration patterns for Indoor GIS
  • Partner with product engineers and managers, UX designers, and development teams to define feasible milestones when the boundary between research, product development, and platform integration is still uncertain
  • Design and develop robust C++, C# and Python components that handle spatial data, imagery, video frames, geometry processing, model evaluation, and quality-review workflows
  • Evaluate and integrate LLMs, multimodal models, embedding/vector search, and computer vision models where they can improve automation, validation, and user experience
  • Create technical specifications, test strategies, benchmark plans, and implementation guidance suitable for AI-assisted coding and spec-driven development workflows
  • Mentor engineers, review designs and code, and help establish engineering standards for maintainable AI/ML, computer vision, and 3D software within Indoor GIS products
  • Communicate technical findings and tradeoffs clearly to engineering leadership and stakeholders, including risks, dependencies, data requirements, performance implications, and integration options
  • Champion spec-driven and AI-assisted development practices across the team
  • Lead code reviews and uphold software quality standards
  • Communicate technical findings, tradeoffs, and progress to both engineering and product audiences

Requirements

  • 5+ years of professional software development experience, with a track record of owning and shipping complex software features
  • Proficiency in two or more of: C++, C#/.NET, Python—with depth in at least one
  • Demonstrated experience integrating or building with AI/ML technologies in production or near-production contexts
  • Strong command of software architecture, algorithms, and data structures
  • Experience with image analysis, computer vision, or 3D/graphics programming
  • Ability to work independently across ambiguous problem spaces and make sound technical judgments
  • Strong communication skills. Able to explain technical tradeoffs to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders
  • Experience mentoring or technically guiding other engineers
  • Experience in AI-driven software development, with AI generating code using Microsoft Copilot, Claude Code, or a similar LLM framework
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related STEM field

Recommended Qualifications

  • Experience with ArcGIS, floor-aware maps, indoor positioning, CAD/BIM/Revit, LiDAR, 360 imagery, or reality capture workflows
  • Experience with Gaussian splats, mesh processing, scene layers, WebGL/DirectX/OpenGL, game engines, or 3D visualization pipelines
  • Experience building RAG systems, semantic search, vector databases, MCP/tool integrations, or agentic workflows for developer or analyst productivity
  • Experience shipping AI-assisted workflows that include user review, confidence scoring, bulk validation, human-in-the-loop correction, and repeatable QA metrics
  • Experience with OpenCV, ONNX, CUDA/GPU acceleration, model benchmarking, or productionizing research code
  • Master’s degree or higher in Computer Science with specialization in Computer Vision, AI/ML, Graphics, Robotics, or a related STEM field

Base salary is one component of our total rewards strategy. Compensation decisions and the base range for this role take into account many factors including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs.

A reasonable estimate of the base salary range is: $123,136 USD - $202,488 USD

• This is a hybrid role out of our Methuen, MA location

This role will serve as the division's subject matter expert for machine vision and automated inspection technologies while contributing to broader automation initiatives that improve quality, efficiency, cost, and manufacturing capacity. This position reports to the Automation Engineering Manager.

You Will Make an Impact By:

  • Designing and implementing machine vision systems that identify, inspect, measure, and evaluate high-precision parts and assemblies.
  • Selecting and integrating industrial cameras, lenses, optics, lighting, and image acquisition hardware for reliable, repeatable inspection performance.
  • Developing image processing and inspection applications using commercial vision platforms and custom software tools.
  • Evaluating traditional image processing and AI/deep learning-based vision solutions where appropriate.
  • Supporting the collection, storage, transformation, and visualization of manufacturing data generated by automation and inspection systems to enable process monitoring, traceability, and continuous improvement.
  • Supporting robotic guidance, alignment, inspection, and measurement applications using 2D and 3D vision technologies.
  • Integrating vision systems with robots, industrial networks, HMIs, SCADA, MES, and manufacturing databases.
  • Supporting machine startup, validation, commissioning, troubleshooting, and continuous improvement of automated machine solutions.
  • Collaborating with manufacturing, quality, engineering, and automation teams in other divisions to standardize vision architectures and best practices to accelerate implementations across global factories.

Skills You Bring:

  • BS degree in electrical engineering and/or computer science is required. Master’s degree specializing in Computer Vision, Image Processing, or a related field is strongly preferred.
  • 2+ years of hands-on experience designing and implementing vison systems in an industrial (clean) manufacturing environment
  • Expertise in selecting, configuring, and integrating vision system hardware to create optimal and repeatable imaging conditions (with high uptime)
  • Mastery of core vision techniques, including image filtering, blob analysis, edge detection, pattern matching, Optical Character Recognition (OCR), and 2D/3D code reading.
  • Proficiency with industry-standard vision software packages (e.g., Cognex VisionPro/In-Sight, Keyence XG-X) and open-source libraries like OpenCV
  • Strong programming skills in Python or C++/C# required for developing custom inspection algorithms and scripting communication between the vision system and other machine controls
  • Experience developing and implementing fiducial-based alignment, position correction, and part localization strategies for automated manufacturing systems.
  • Familiarity with industrial networking protocols (EtherNet/IP, EtherCAT, etc.) and automated data collection systems (SCADA, MES)
  • Experience working with manufacturing data systems, databases, data pipelines, and analytics tools (SQL, Power BI/Fabric, Python, AWS).

Compensation and Benefits:

Salary Pay Range: $ 75,000.00 - 110,000.00 per year. This range is a good faith estimate of the expected salary range for this position, based on a wide range of factors including qualifications, experience and training, operational and business needs and other considerations permitted by law.

Bonus: This position is eligible for a discretionary annual bonus, in an amount to be determined by MKS [or as applicable].

Benefits: MKS offers a comprehensive benefits package, including health insurance coverage (medical, dental and vision), 401(k) with company match, life and disability insurance, 12 paid holidays, sick time, 15 paid vacation days, [6 weeks fully paid] parental leave, adoption assistance and tuition reimbursement [and for participation in any stock programs, signing bonus, etc.

MKS is an equal opportunity employer, including disability, veteran status and all categories protected by law. Please review our EOE statements for additional details. MKS is generally only hiring candidates who reside in states where we are registered to do business.

The Sr. AI Engineer, Device Intelligence will be a key member of the Danaher Autonomous and Intelligent Labs team, reporting to its Vice President. This new role is instrumental in the implementation of cutting-edge AI systems that leverage data created by Danaher devices to extract meaningful insights and dramatically improve user experience, with the goal of upleveling Danaher's devices across Life Sciences, Diagnostics and Biotechnology sectors. This position is remote in Eastern US.

In This Role, You Will Have The Opportunity To

  • Collaborate with the VP and the broader team to develop Enterprise grade capabilities and platforms enable the creation of intelligent instruments and autonomous labs.
  • Design and implement advanced AI systems, including next-generation multi-level and multi-domain agentic systems, to enhance instrument intelligence and lab automation, upleveling user capabilities.

Collaborate with business stakeholders, technical experts, and subject matter experts to build comprehensive AI roadmaps for imaging products across various verticals.

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, electrical engineering, robotics, automation, life sciences or a related field. An advanced degree (MS or PhD) in a relevant area (i.e. Neural Networks, Foundation Model, Agentic Workflows, Machine Learning, Computer Vision, Robotics) is preferred.

Demonstrable expertise with at least 3 of the following: convolutional neural networks, foundation models, vector databases, AI evaluation methods, RAG approaches, agentic frameworks, robotics.

Including the use of genAI and agentic systems for coding. Experience with cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Google Cloud, Azure) and familiarity with hardware acceleration technologies (e.g. TPUs, GPUs, ARM-CPUs).
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams, communicate complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, and align AI development with product goals and roadmaps.

  • Experience with regulatory processes, especially for medical devices and AI/ML-based software as a medical device (SaMD).

descriptionHtml:
Who We Are

Aurelius is the autonomous directed energy company.

We are a group of engineers, operators, and company patriots building American-made, laser-based counter-UAS systems that neutralize aerial threats.

Archimedes, our autonomous laser turret, combines a high-power laser with radar and machine vision to find, track, and defeat small drones. We design in San Francisco, manufacture in Detroit, and test onsite, on our own cUAS range.

The Role

You’ll own perception for Archimedes: turning live EO/IR and other sensor data into reliable detection and tracking on a moving, edge-deployed system.

This is a hands-on role across the full ML pipeline. You’ll make decisions about data, train and evaluate models, deploy them on embedded compute, and use range results to decide what to improve next. The immediate work is improving the resilience of an existing perception pipeline; as more systems are deployed, field data will create new opportunities to improve performance.

You’ll work directly with robotics software, controls, and hardware engineers and help mentor perception engineers as the team grows.

Must-Haves

  • Personally trained, evaluated, and deployed detection, tracking, or segmentation models on a physical system or live sensor stream.
  • Hands-on multi-object tracking and state estimation (Kalman filters, IMM, data association, track management) on real sensor data.
  • Worked across the robotics ML pipeline: data, training, evaluation, deployment, and improvement from real-world results.
  • Strong Python and comfortable reading and writing C++, including the path from trained model to on-device inference
  • Experience measuring and improving performance against real-time latency and compute constraints.
  • U.S. citizenship, as required for this role’s export-controlled work.

First 6 Months

  • Define the perception architecture across detection, tracking, classification, and EO/IR fusion, documented and agreed with controls and robotics software.
  • Build a repeatable pipeline for turning range captures, hard negatives, and field failures into training and evaluation improvements.
  • Establish on-device latency and performance baselines, then improve them.
  • Diagnose and address early field failure modes, including tiny targets, clutter, ego-motion, and track handoff to controls.
  • Work alongside hardware and controls engineers on range days to validate changes on the system.

Nice to Haves

  • EO/IR perception, radar-camera fusion, or small aerial targets.
  • Hands-on with current detector families like YOLO and RT-DETR.
  • Data strategies for physical systems, including sim-to-real or fine-tuning on field data.
  • JAX or PyTorch experience with robotics models.
  • On-device inference optimization against a measured latency budget.
  • Distinctive, self-directed projects that solved a specific technical gap.

Not a Fit If

  • Your recent work is mainly language models, recommenders, ranking, search, ads, or tabular forecasting, or offline batch work with no on-device deployment
  • Your background is research only, with no deployment on physical hardware
  • You’ve worked only on one narrow part of the pipeline and don’t want to own the broader perception problem
  • You need remote or hybrid work

How We Work

At Aurelius we work what we call, 5+X. Our core operating hours are 5 days a week, Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm Pacific Time.

The X is the honest acknowledgment that hard work sometimes takes more. That can be late nights and weekends during sprints and ramp-up periods or conferences, deployments, and events when the mission calls for it.

This role is onsite 5 days a week in San Francisco.

Benefits

At Aurelius Systems, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package is available at little to no cost to employees and supports health, recovery, and whatever comes next. Explore Our Benefits.

Export Control Notice

This role requires access to export-controlled information or items and requires U.S. citizenship.

Not a Perfect Fit?

Email our Head of Talent, alfredo@aureliussystems.us with the most extraordinary thing you've built or done.

Compensation Range: $190K - $222K

Boston Dynamics is building the world’s most advanced robots. The Spot robot performs inspections on thousands of sites around the world, helping customers to inspect, operate and optimize their industrial facilities.

descriptionHtml:
About LightSpeed

LightSpeed Build Technologies is revolutionizing the construction industry through AI-powered robotics. Our flagship systems—BRUTE for automated wall panel manufacturing and DEX for on-site collaborative construction—are addressing the global housing crisis by delivering unprecedented speed, precision, and affordability in homebuilding.

Position Overview

As Senior World Sensing Engineer, you will own how LightSpeed's robots sense and understand the world. You will architect the sensor array on every robot, from cameras and lidar to force-torque and process sensors, and the pipeline that turns those signals into one trusted world model: where everything really is, what state it is in, and how sure we are.

What You'll Work On

Sensor array and pipeline

  • Define the sensor suite for every robot family across factory cells, mobile DEX and roof configurations, and upgrade it when a trade needs a signal we don't yet sense:
    • Vision: wrist RGB-D and stereo for close-range manipulation, cell and head cameras for scene coverage, global-shutter cameras for fast motion
    • Lidar: 3D lidar for mapping, localization and site safety on mobile robots
    • Contact: 6-axis force-torque at each wrist, tactile sensing on grippers and hands
    • Proprioception: joint encoders, motor current and IMU on arms, bases and the gantry
    • Tool and process: laser line profilers and time-of-flight for surface, gap and depth; tool state, flow and pressure for nailers, pumps and spray
    • Site and safety: safety-rated area scanners, and site positioning such as a total station or UWB where lidar alone isn't enough
  • Own sensor selection, position and orientation on every robot, for coverage, occlusion and changing light; the application team handles mounting and protection against dust and overspray
  • Own time synchronization across every sensor, robot state and teleoperation stream
  • Own the calibration strategy (intrinsic, extrinsic, hand-eye, camera-lidar) and keep it reliable through tool changes and daily operation
  • Build the sensor data pipeline: capture, streaming, compression and logging at rate, delivered to the world model, teleoperation and robot learning
  • Monitor sensor health and detect drift before it affects a task

World model

  • Design the world model: an element graph keyed to BIM, poses with uncertainty, and the state of every element (planned, placed, fastened, verified, failed)
  • Register the BIM to the as-built, to tool tolerance, for panels in the factory and for rooms on site
  • Build sensor fusion and localization so mobile robots know where they are relative to the building, not just a map
  • Keep element state current from perception and from the verification results of every primitive
  • Own the world-model interface that the planner, primitives and teaching pipeline use, designed so more than one robot can share it

Perception

  • Set the direction for a generalized perception model: one shared model for geometry and categories that learns new features from a few examples
  • Build measurement for material state: cable and tape position, mud and surface flatness, foam depth, fastener seating
  • Build object detection, segmentation and 6-DoF pose estimation for parts, tools and fasteners in cluttered, confined and poorly lit spaces
  • Set accuracy targets tied to task success, and build the benchmarks that measure them
  • Deploy perception at the edge within a defined latency budget

Foundation and skill pipeline

  • Co-own the foundation interfaces with the robot learning and agentic planning principals, and own the world-model interface
  • Add the features and sensing each new trade needs as it moves through the skill pipeline
  • Measure success by how fast a new trade can be taught
  • Decide with the robot learning principal what data is collected and how failures are labelled

Technical leadership

  • Set sensing and perception architecture across both robot families
  • Mentor perception and sensing engineers
  • Make the system something engineers can teach new trades with, without you in the loop
  • Stay hands-on: write production code and test on real robots every week

Required qualifications

Sensing and world modeling

  • 5+ years building perception, sensing or state estimation for physical robots or autonomous systems, with systems deployed in production
  • Architected a multi-sensor suite end to end: selection, placement, synchronization, calibration and the data pipeline
  • Deep expertise in 3D vision and geometry: multi-view geometry, point cloud registration, SLAM and sensor fusion across cameras, lidar and IMU
  • Built a world or scene representation that planning or control consumed, not only detectors
  • Deep learning for perception in PyTorch, from dataset to deployed model

Engineering and leadership

  • Strong C++ and Python
  • Experience with ROS2, Linux, Docker and CI/CD workflows
  • A record of setting technical direction across teams and mentoring senior engineers

Preferred qualifications

  • MS or PhD in Robotics, Computer Vision, Computer Science or a related field
  • Scan-to-CAD or scan-to-BIM comparison, as-built verification or digital twins
  • World modeling, mapping or localization on an autonomous vehicle or field robotics team
  • Perception for manipulation, including deformable objects or surface measurement
  • Vision foundation models such as SAM, DINOv2 or FoundationPose
  • Observation spaces for imitation learning or vision-language-action policies
  • Sensor data for robot learning datasets, such as MCAP or rosbag
  • Hardware time sync (PTP, hardware triggers), CUDA, TensorRT and edge deployment on NVIDIA Jetson
  • Simulation and synthetic data with Isaac Sim, MuJoCo or similar
  • A shared world model across multiple robots
  • Background in construction, manufacturing or industrial automation

Why Join LightSpeed

  • Build the senses and the world model of robots that are addressing the housing crisis
  • Own sensing end to end, from sensor selection to the world model every robot reads
  • Work on rare real-world problems: as-built registration at tool tolerance, deformable materials, dusty and confined sites, factory and field robots on one stack
  • Hands-on culture with direct access to robots, sensors and manufacturing environments
  • Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits

Employment Relationship

descriptionText:
About LightSpeed

LightSpeed Build Technologies is revolutionizing the construction industry through AI-powered robotics. Our flagship systems—BRUTE for automated wall panel manufacturing and DEX for on-site collaborative construction—are addressing the global housing crisis by delivering unprecedented speed, precision, and affordability in homebuilding.

Position Overview

As Senior World Sensing Engineer, you will own how LightSpeed's robots sense and understand the world. You will architect the sensor array on every robot, from cameras and lidar to force-torque and process sensors, and the pipeline that turns those signals into one trusted world model: where everything really is, what state it is in, and how sure we are.

What You'll Work On

Sensor array and pipeline



- Define the sensor suite for every robot family across factory cells, mobile DEX and roof configurations, and upgrade it when a trade needs a signal we don't yet sense:

- Vision: wrist RGB-D and stereo for close-range manipulation, cell and head cameras for scene coverage, global-shutter cameras for fast motion
- Lidar: 3D lidar for mapping, localization and site safety on mobile robots
- Contact: 6-axis force-torque at each wrist, tactile sensing on grippers and hands
- Proprioception: joint encoders, motor current and IMU on arms, bases and the gantry
- Tool and process: laser line profilers and time-of-flight for surface, gap and depth; tool state, flow and pressure for nailers, pumps and spray
- Site and safety: safety-rated area scanners, and site positioning such as a total station or UWB where lidar alone isn't enough
- Own sensor selection, position and orientation on every robot, for coverage, occlusion and changing light; the application team handles mounting and protection against dust and overspray
- Own time synchronization across every sensor, robot state and teleoperation stream
- Own the calibration strategy (intrinsic, extrinsic, hand-eye, camera-lidar) and keep it reliable through tool changes and daily operation
- Build the sensor data pipeline: capture, streaming, compression and logging at rate, delivered to the world model, teleoperation and robot learning
- Monitor sensor health and detect drift before it affects a task

World model



- Design the world model: an element graph keyed to BIM, poses with uncertainty, and the state of every element (planned, placed, fastened, verified, failed)
- Register the BIM to the as-built, to tool tolerance, for panels in the factory and for rooms on site
- Build sensor fusion and localization so mobile robots know where they are relative to the building, not just a map
- Keep element state current from perception and from the verification results of every primitive
- Own the world-model interface that the planner, primitives and teaching pipeline use, designed so more than one robot can share it

Perception



- Set the direction for a generalized perception model: one shared model for geometry and categories that learns new features from a few examples
- Build measurement for material state: cable and tape position, mud and surface flatness, foam depth, fastener seating
- Build object detection, segmentation and 6-DoF pose estimation for parts, tools and fasteners in cluttered, confined and poorly lit spaces
- Set accuracy targets tied to task success, and build the benchmarks that measure them
- Deploy perception at the edge within a defined latency budget

Foundation and skill pipeline



- Co-own the foundation interfaces with the robot learning and agentic planning principals, and own the world-model interface
- Add the features and sensing each new trade needs as it moves through the skill pipeline
- Measure success by how fast a new trade can be taught
- Decide with the robot learning principal what data is collected and how failures are labelled

Technical leadership



- Set sensing and perception architecture across both robot families
- Mentor perception and sensing engineers
- Make the system something engineers can teach new trades with, without you in the loop
- Stay hands-on: write production code and test on real robots every week

Required qualifications

Sensing and world modeling



- 5+ years building perception, sensing or state estimation for physical robots or autonomous systems, with systems deployed in production
- Architected a multi-sensor suite end to end: selection, placement, synchronization, calibration and the data pipeline
- Deep expertise in 3D vision and geometry: multi-view geometry, point cloud registration, SLAM and sensor fusion across cameras, lidar and IMU
- Built a world or scene representation that planning or control consumed, not only detectors
- Deep learning for perception in PyTorch, from dataset to deployed model

Engineering and leadership



- Strong C++ and Python
- Experience with ROS2, Linux, Docker and CI/CD workflows
- A record of setting technical direction across teams and mentoring senior engineers

Preferred qualifications



- MS or PhD in Robotics, Computer Vision, Computer Science or a related field
- Scan-to-CAD or scan-to-BIM comparison, as-built verification or digital twins
- World modeling, mapping or localization on an autonomous vehicle or field robotics team
- Perception for manipulation, including deformable objects or surface measurement
- Vision foundation models such as SAM, DINOv2 or FoundationPose
- Observation spaces for imitation learning or vision-language-action policies
- Sensor data for robot learning datasets, such as MCAP or rosbag
- Hardware time sync (PTP, hardware triggers), CUDA, TensorRT and edge deployment on NVIDIA Jetson
- Simulation and synthetic data with Isaac Sim, MuJoCo or similar
- A shared world model across multiple robots
- Background in construction, manufacturing or industrial automation

Why Join LightSpeed



- Build the senses and the world model of robots that are addressing the housing crisis
- Own sensing end to end, from sensor selection to the world model every robot reads
- Work on rare real-world problems: as-built registration at tool tolerance, deformable materials, dusty and confined sites, factory and field robots on one stack
- Hands-on culture with direct access to robots, sensors and manufacturing environments
- Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits

This position is at-will, meaning either you or the Company may terminate employment at any time, with or without cause or notice.

LightSpeed Build Technologies is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome candidates from all backgrounds and experiences.

descriptionHtml:
At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we envision a future where technology helps humanity thrive. Our world-class teams work across disciplines and collaborate with leading universities to advance research in AI, human happiness, robotics, driving, and materials science, helping shape the future of mobility, amplify human ability, and make our lives safer and more sustainable.



The Learning From Videos (LFV) team develops world foundation models that leverage large-scale multi-modal data (RGB, depth, flow, semantics, actions, tactile, audio, etc.) from multiple domains to power downstream embodied AI tasks. Our topics of interest include Video Generation, World Models, 4D Reconstruction, Multi-Modal Models, Multi-View Geometry, Data Augmentation, and Video-Language-Action models, with a primary focus on embodied applications such as robotics and driving. We are making progress on some of the hardest scientific challenges around spatio-temporal reasoning, and how it can lead to the deployment of autonomous agents in real-world unstructured environments.


 


Our team is looking for a Research Engineer to help develop and deploy our world foundation models (WFMs) toward their key milestones in the autonomous driving domain. As our WFMs scale in both capability and ambition, we need a strong engineer who can bridge the gap between research ideas and production-grade systems. This is not a traditional software engineering role; you will work directly alongside research scientists, understand the research deeply enough to make independent technical decisions, and play a key role in enabling the deployment of key research breakthroughs into close-to-production environments.


 


As a Research Engineer, you will be responsible for supporting and optimizing large-scale distributed training of diffusion and transformer models; maintaining the infrastructure that ingests, unifies, and serves heterogeneous multi-modal datasets at scale; and developing tools and pipelines that accelerate the research-to-results cycle. You will work closely with researchers to prototype new ideas, run experiments, and help ship our most successful models toward real-world applications with real-world impact.


This role requires close collaboration with multiple TRI divisions (Robotics, Automated Driving, Human-Interactive Driving, etc.) as well external Toyota and University partners, and the ability to reconcile and prioritize possibly competing requirements in a fast-paced combination of research and production environments.



Responsibilities


  • Collaborate directly with research scientists to implement, iterate on, and evaluate new architectures, objectives, datasets, and training strategies. Translate research prototypes into clean, maintainable, reusable code that will be shared across multiple TRI teams and the broader Toyota ecosystem.




  • Build and maintain scalable pipelines for ingesting, converting, validating, and serving heterogeneous datasets (multi-view, multi-modal, multi-embodiment, etc.), across robotics and autonomous driving, into unified training-ready formats. Track and integrate new public and internal datasets as they become available.




  • Support and optimize large-scale distributed training of world foundation models on multi-GPU and multi-node clusters. Manage experiment workflows, profiling, debugging, and hyperparameter sweeps to ensure optimal performance in a timely manner.




  • Develop tools for dataset inspection, experiment tracking, model evaluation, GPU resource management, and visualization. Automate repetitive workflows to improve team velocity.




  • Work with other TRI teams and Toyota affiliates to set up shared pipelines, onboard their data, and support joint training and evaluation efforts.




  • Produce maintainable, well-documented code. Contribute to internal tooling and open-source releases to the scientific community.






Qualifications


  • Master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related field, with a minimum of 3 years of relevant experience and strong software engineering skills.




  • Deep proficiency in Python, PyTorch, and the Unix/Linux toolchain. Comfort working in terminal-heavy, SSH-based workflows on shared GPU clusters.




  • Hands-on experience with large-scale deep learning training, including distributed training (DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, or similar), GPU profiling, and debugging training failures at scale.




  • Experience building data pipelines for heterogeneous or multi-modal datasets (images, video, depth, point clouds, actions, etc).




  • Experience with video diffusion models, 3D/4D reconstruction, and multi-view geometry.




  • You are proactive, self-directed, and comfortable operating with ambiguity in a research-driven environment that spans multiple divisions.




  • You are a reliable teammate who communicates clearly and takes ownership of problems end-to-end.






Bonus Qualifications

  • Experience with cloud training infrastructure (AWS SageMaker, EC2) and containerized workflows (Docker, Kubernetes)


  • Familiarity with standard data formats and collection pipelines (ROS, MCAP, HDF5, etc.) as well as simulation environments.




  • Proficiency with modern AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code) for accelerating engineering workflows.




  • Track record of contributions to open-source projects or publications at top venues (CVPR, ICLR, NeurIPS, RSS, ICRA, etc.) is a plus but not required.








Please include links to any relevant open-source contributions or technical project write-ups with your application.


 


The pay range for this position at commencement of employment is expected to be between $180,000 and $258,750/year for California-based roles. Base pay offered will depend on multiple individualized factors, including, but not limited to, a candidate's experience, skills, job-related knowledge, and market location. TRI offers a generous benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401(k) eligibility, paid time off benefits (including vacation, sick time, and parental leave), and an annual cash bonus structure. Additional details regarding these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment.

Ventures GP, L.P., and the purposes for which we use such personal information.


 


TRI is fueled by a diverse and inclusive community of people with unique backgrounds, education and life experiences. We are dedicated to fostering an innovative and collaborative environment by living the values that are an essential part of our culture. We believe diversity makes us stronger and are proud to provide Equal Employment Opportunity for all, without regard to an applicant’s race, color, creed, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, religion, marital status, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected under federal, state or local laws.

An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records for employment.

descriptionHtml:
Latitude AI (lat.ai) is building the future of Ford’s autonomy roadmap to make travel safer, less stressful, and more enjoyable for everyone. Bringing this vision to scale, our fully in-house developed hands-free ADAS platform will debut on the all-new Ford Fathom in 2027.

When you join the Latitude team, you’ll work alongside leading experts across machine learning and robotics, cloud platforms, mapping, sensors and compute systems, test operations, systems and safety engineering – all dedicated to redefining the relationship between people and their vehicles for millions of customers.

As a Ford Motor Company subsidiary, we operate independently to develop automated driving technology at the speed of a technology startup. Latitude is headquartered in Pittsburgh with engineering centers in Dearborn, Mich., and Palo Alto, Calif.

Meet The Team

The Unified Model development team is a group of highly skilled and experienced professionals who specialize in cutting-edge computer vision and machine learning technology. Together, we collaborate to create advanced detection models that are capable of generating representations of both static and dynamic actors. These representations are then utilized by various downstream autonomy consumers including motion planning, prediction, and localization.

The team's primary focus is on developing compute-efficient, multi-view, multi-sensor deep learning models that can perform a wide range of tasks such as 3D object detection, lane line detection, state estimation, and scene segmentation. The ultimate goal is to take these algorithms from the lab to the road, ensuring that they are optimized for onboard performance and able to function as production-grade vision systems on vehicles.

To achieve this goal, the team constantly stays up-to-date with the latest research literature and pushes the boundaries of what is possible. We are dedicated to developing cutting-edge ML algorithms and models that can help vehicles reason about the world around them in real-time.

What You’ll Do

  • Develop spatio-temporal machine learning models for detection, multi-sensor fusion, segmentation, etc.
  • Read literature, analyze raw data, and design state-of-the-art solutions
  • Transition solutions from the lab to the test track and public roads to ensure successful production-level implementation.
  • Collaborate with perception experts and experienced roboticists on algorithm design, prototyping, testing, deployment, and productization
  • Build and maintain industry-leading software practices and principles
  • Develop clean and efficient software for perception modules interfacing with other key modules
  • Show initiative and be a valued team member in a fast-paced, innovative, and entrepreneurial environment

What You'll Need To Succeed

  • A Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field plus 7 years of industry experience.
  • Expert-level knowledge and experience in machine learning, with a proven track record of developing and deploying deep learning solutions using PyTorch, Tensorflow, or similar frameworks
  • Experience in developing perception systems using sensors such as Camera, Radar, and LiDAR
  • Strong experience in computer vision, perception, and point cloud processing
  • Proven experience in shipping computer vision software products to industry or consumers
  • At least 5 years of development experience in Python/C++ environments.

Level and title will ultimately be determined based on experience and interview performance.

Nice To Have (optional)

  • Ph.D. with machine learning focus, or equivalent experience
  • Experience developing and deploying temporal computer vision models (for instance, video activity recognition or using multiple frames for improved results on other tasks).

Uber is launching AV Labs to accelerate the autonomous technology ecosystem. descriptionHtml:
About Mecka AI

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.

We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.

We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

The role

Mecka captures how people move, work and interact with the physical world. The footage is messy: hands disappear behind objects, cameras turn quickly, and motion blur hides the details. You’ll build models that make sense of it—and turn it into accurate 3D data that robotics teams can train on.

We’re looking for machine learning engineers with depth in pose estimation, SLAM or 3D reconstruction who want to own what happens after the experiment works. You’ll train models, investigate where they fail and get them running reliably in production, working across the perception stack along the way.

What you’ll do

  • Build models for the problems in front of us. You’ll train vision models from scratch on large multi-view, multi-sensor datasets, developing new losses and architectures where existing methods fall short.
  • Work through the difficult footage. You’ll tackle motion blur, fast rotation, heavy occlusion and partial views of hands, bodies and objects.
  • Find out where your models fail. You’ll evaluate them on our own video, measuring real error and failure rates alongside public benchmark results.
  • Own the path to production. You’ll optimize GPU performance, make results reproducible, integrate models into our data pipeline and ship releases you can roll back.
  • Follow problems through to a fix. You’ll reproduce customer-reported issues, understand what went wrong and deliver a fix. You’ll also prototype quickly as new perception problems come up.

What you’ll bring

  • Strong machine learning fundamentals. You’re comfortable building and training models with Python and PyTorch.
  • Experience training large vision models from scratch. Your experience goes beyond running or fine-tuning existing models.
  • Depth in a computer vision specialty. You’ve worked deeply in at least one area, such as pose estimation, SLAM or 3D reconstruction.
  • Experience owning models in production. You’ve shipped a model or perception component and stayed responsible for it afterward.
  • Comfort with the work as it is. You can make progress with noisy real-world data and adapt when priorities shift.

Nice to have

Experience in one or more of these areas would be valuable:

  • Hand and body tracking: 3D hand and full-body tracking, mesh recovery, human-object and human-scene interaction, and estimating contact with objects and the ground.
  • SLAM, VIO and calibration: Learned ego-motion, optical flow, online calibration and metric scale.
  • 3D reconstruction and objects: Feed-forward or per-scene reconstruction, Gaussian splatting or NeRF, and neural 3D object estimation from egocentric video.

If you don't check every box above but believe you can do the job, we encourage you to apply — we're looking for capability and trajectory, not a perfect checklist match.

We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, we will partner with you to meet your needs.

We may use AI-assisted tools to help evaluate applications against the requirements of this role. These tools support our recruiting team in identifying qualified candidates but do not replace human judgment or limit which applications may be reviewed or considered.

Compensation Range: CA$140K - CA$200K

companyDescription:
ACV is a high growth technology company that provides a vibrant digital marketplace for wholesale vehicle transactions and data services. ACV's marketplace called ACV Auctions offers transparent and accurate vehicle information to customers powered by technology innovations and data insights. 

On a mission to build and enable the most trusted and efficient digital marketplaces for buying and selling used vehicles, ACV’s platform leverages data insights and technology to power its digital marketplace and data services, enabling dealers and commercial partners to buy, sell and value vehicles with confidence and efficiency. ACV’s network of brands includes ACV Auctions, ACV Transportation and ACV Capital within its Marketplace Products as well as True360, ACV Data Services and MAX Digital.
descriptionHtml:
If you are looking for a career at a dynamic company with a people-first mindset and a deep culture of growth and autonomy, ACV is the right place for you! Competitive compensation packages and learning and development opportunities, ACV has what you need to advance to the next level in your career. We will continue to raise the bar every day by investing in our people and technology to help our customers succeed. We hire people who share our passion, bring innovative ideas to the table, and enjoy a collaborative atmosphere.

Who we are:

ACV is a technology company that has revolutionized how dealers buy and sell cars online. We are transforming the automotive industry. ACV Auctions Inc. (ACV), has applied innovation and user-designed, data driven applications and solutions. We are building the most trusted and efficient digital marketplace with data solutions for sourcing, selling and managing used vehicles with transparency and comprehensive insights that were once unimaginable. We are disruptors of the industry and we want you to join us on our journey. Our network of brands include ACV Auctions, ACV Transportation, ClearCar, MAX Digital and ACV Capital within its Marketplace Products, as well as, True360 and Data Services.

At ACV we focus on the Health, Physical, Financial, Social and Emotional Wellness of our Teammates and, to support this, we offer:

  • Multiple medical plans including a high deductible, low cost health plan
  • Company-sponsored (paid) Short-Term Disability, Long-Term Disability, and Life Insurance
  • Comprehensive optional benefits such as Dental, Vision, Supplemental Life/AD&D, Legal/ID Protection, and Accident and Critical Illness Insurance
  • Generous paid time off options, including uncapped vacation days, the greater of 3 paid sick days or in accordance with the applicable state or local paid sick leave law, 6 paid company holidays, 2 floating holidays, parental leave, bereavement leave, jury duty leave, voting leave, and other forms of paid leave as required by applicable law or regulation
  • Employee Stock Purchase Program with additional opportunities to earn stock in the Company
  • Retirement planning through the Company’s 401(k)

What you will do:

ACV's Machine Learning organization is looking for a talented Machine Learning Engineer III to join our ML inspection team. In this role, you'll drive end-to-end computer vision solutions processing hundreds of thousands of vehicle inspections annually into reliable, actionable insights, directly reducing inspection turnaround time, improving valuation accuracy, and scaling the capabilities of our inspection platform. You'll design and train damage detection models while architecting the high-throughput serving infrastructure needed to keep those models performant under real production loads. As ACV continues to grow, you'll play a direct role in ensuring our inspection capabilities remain accurate, efficient, and resilient at scale.

This role goes beyond executing on a defined roadmap. You'll identify opportunities, shape solutions end-to-end, and take ownership of outcomes. You connect the dots between stakeholder needs and what's technically feasible, bringing recommendations grounded in both theory and practical constraints. When you hear a narrow question, you think about the broader system it lives in and build toward that.

The core responsibilities of this role are:

  • Design and train high-performance computer vision models for automated damage detection, focusing on precision, recall, and model robustness.
  • Architect and maintain high-throughput, containerized microservices for model serving using REST/gRPC to ensure low-latency performance.
  • Collaborate with business stakeholders to translate complex inspection requirements into scalable, production-grade ML solutions.
  • Own the end-to-end model lifecycle, from experimentation and design to deployment and optimization in high-traffic environments.
  • Design and maintain robust data pipelines using Kafka to ensure high-fidelity inputs for model serving and inference.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications:

  • Graduate education (MS or PhD) in a computationally intensive domain or equivalent work experience.
  • 3+ years of prior computer vision experience
  • Advanced proficiency with Computer Vision frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, OpenCV, TensorFlow) and Python/SQL.
  • Experience designing and maintaining visual data annotation pipelines and evaluation frameworks for complex, real-world image datasets.
  • Experience optimizing high-latency models for real-time inference
  • Backend software engineering experience in the cloud (AWS / GCP) with a focus on microservices (docker) and the ML model development lifecycle.
  • Experience building and maintaining streaming data pipelines (e.g., Kafka) for real-time model serving.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Knowledge of ML frameworks and libraries, such as Kubeflow, Databricks, KServe and so on
  • Experience designing evaluation frameworks for complex visual data

Our Values

Trust & Transparency | People First | Positive Experiences | Calm Persistence | Never Settling

At ACV, we are committed to an inclusive culture in which every individual is welcomed and empowered to celebrate their true selves. We achieve this by fostering a work environment of acceptance and understanding that is free from discrimination. ACV is committed to being an equal opportunity employer regardless of sex, race, creed, color, religion, marital status, national origin, age, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, disability, military status, status as a veteran, or any other protected characteristic. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. If you have a disability or special need that requires reasonable accommodation, please let us know.

For information on our collection and use of your personal information, please see our Privacy Notice.

No immigration or work visa sponsorship provided for this position.

Compensation: The compensation range for this position is listed in the "Job Details" section at the bottom of this posting. Please note that final compensation will be determined based upon the applicant's relevant experience, skill set, location, business needs, market demands, and other factors as permitted by law.

descriptionHtml:
Voyager is an innovative space, defense, and national security technology company committed to advancing and delivering transformative, mission-critical solutions. We tackle the most complex challenges to unlock new frontiers for human progress, fortify national security, and protect critical assets to lead in the race for technological and operational superiority from ground to space.

Forge the Future: Join Voyager Technologies

The future belongs to those who build it. At Voyager Technologies, we’re building technologies that protect lives, expand frontiers and prepare us for what’s next. And we’re doing that with people who are wired to solve, build, adapt and lead. These roles are not for the faint of heart. 

You’ll help lay the foundation for humanity's future. Join a culture where innovation thrives, curiosity is rewarded, and impact is real. We’re a company of doers, thinkers and builders, united by purpose and grounded in reality.

If you want to put your skills to work where the stakes are real and the mission is bigger than any one person, forge the future with Voyager.

The Company is currently seeking Machine Learning Engineers who can develop cutting edge Deep Learning technologies applied to pressing problems in the domain of Computer Vision, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), and Geospatial Exploitation. You will have considerable responsibility, and your role will have direct impact on relevant issues facing the United States government customers.

This posting stays open continuously. We hire machine learning engineers at several levels, from early career to senior staff, and review applications on a rolling basis. Your level and title are determined during the hiring process, based on your experience and the scope of your past work. See Levels We Hire For below.

This position is based in El Segundo, CA. If your experience aligns with our required qualifications and you are inspired by our mission, we’d like to connect. If you don’t see the right role right now, Join Our Talent Community and stay connected as we continue to build what’s next.

In This Role, The Essential Functions Are

We hire at five levels; each row shows the typical experience and scope.

Title

Typical experience

Scope

Machine Learning Engineer I

0–2 years

Implements models and ML pipelines under guidance. Usually holds a BS or MS and may have internship or research experience.

Machine Learning Engineer II

2–5 years

Independently develops and deploys ML solutions. Can take an ML problem from requirements through implementation, including production deployment, model monitoring, feature engineering and experimentation.

Senior Machine Learning Engineer

5–8 years

Owns complex ML systems and technical projects. Makes architecture decisions, mentors junior engineers, and works closely with product, data and platform teams.

Staff Machine Learning Engineer

8–12+ years

Provides technical leadership across teams and systems, beyond simply owning larger individual projects. Defines architecture and technical direction across multiple teams and influences engineering standards and ML strategy.

Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer

12–15+ years

Sets organization-wide technical strategy and architecture. Responsible for very large technical problems and/or company-wide ML architecture and strategy.

At Every Level, You Will

  • Research, conceive, design, prototype and/or implement advanced Deep Neural Network Architectures as well as other relevant Machine Learning models.
  • Apply deep learning algorithms to train neural networks for object detection and classification.
  • Develop domain-aware pre-processing algorithms, and other methods to increase model generalization.
  • Apply signal pre-processing techniques on SAR data.
  • Create physics simulations of various phenomenologies and develop methods to account for bias between simulated and real-world data.
  • Develop appropriate objective functions and sound performance assessment plans.
  • Present work at meetings and conferences.
  • Develop and deliver production-quality code (mainly Python).

As you move up in level, responsibilities build on those above:

  • Machine Learning Engineer II and above: independently take machine learning problems from requirements through implementation, including production deployment, model monitoring, feature engineering and experimentation.
  • Senior Machine Learning Engineer and above: own complex machine learning systems and technical projects, make architecture decisions, mentor junior engineers, and work closely with product, data and platform teams.
  • Staff Machine Learning Engineer and above: provide technical leadership across teams and systems, define architecture and technical direction across multiple teams, and influence engineering standards and ML strategy.
  • Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer: set organization-wide technical strategy and architecture, and own very large technical problems and/or company-wide ML architecture and strategy.

If your experience aligns with our basic qualifications and you are inspired by our mission, we’d like to connect. If you don’t see the right role right now, Join Our Talent Community and stay connected as we continue to build what’s next.

  • Qualifications build by level: each level includes everything from the level before it, plus the items listed. Years shown are years of applicable experience.

Machine Learning Engineer I (0–2 years)

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related field.

Machine Learning Engineer II (2–5 years): all Machine Learning Engineer I qualifications, plus:

  • Experience independently taking an ML problem from requirements through implementation.
  • Experience with production deployment, model monitoring, feature engineering and experimentation.

Senior Machine Learning Engineer (5–8 years): all Machine Learning Engineer II qualifications, plus:

  • A record of owning complex ML systems and technical projects.
  • Experience making architecture decisions and mentoring junior engineers.
  • Experience partnering with product, data and platform teams.

Staff Machine Learning Engineer (8–12+ years): all Senior Machine Learning Engineer qualifications, plus:

  • A record of technical leadership across teams and systems, beyond owning larger individual projects.
  • Experience defining architecture and technical direction across multiple teams.
  • Experience influencing engineering standards and ML strategy.

Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineer (12–15+ years): all Staff Machine Learning Engineer qualifications, plus:

  • A record of setting organization-wide technical strategy and architecture.
  • Experience owning very large technical problems and/or company-wide ML architecture and strategy.
  • Experience developing or guiding advanced machine learning, signal-processing and exploitation algorithms, and leading technical efforts across organizational and disciplinary boundaries.
  • Ability to evaluate unfamiliar sensors and datasets using first-principles reasoning.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical concepts to expert and non-expert audiences, mentor senior technical staff, and operate effectively with limited direction.

Preferred Qualifications

These apply across all levels.

  • Master’s degree or PhD.
  • Strong background in Machine Learning (preferably Deep Neural Networks).
  • Need to be flexible in a small business environment.
  • Familiarity with radar sensing phenomenology.
  • Open Source frameworks is a huge plus.
  • Ability to program in multiple languages (Python, Matlab, C/C++).
  • Experience connecting physics-based signal processing with machine learning, computer vision, or automated exploitation.
  • Expertise in areas such as target detection and recognition, geolocation, or multimodal fusion.

Travel, Physical And/or Government Mandated Requirements

  • Ability to obtain and maintain a US Government Security Clearance

The good faith base salary range for this role is $120,000 - $280,000 at the time of this posting. Where you fall within the range depends on your experience, skills, and location. This range reflects base salary only and does not include benefits or bonus/incentive. This range may be adjusted in the future.

Voyager offers a highly competitive total compensation package designed to support the well-being, growth, and success of our employees. Employees benefit from a flexible and comprehensive rewards program that supports both professional and personal well-being.

  • Flexible Time Off (FTO), empowering employees to take the time they need to recharge and maintain a healthy work-life balance
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and their families, with a significant portion of premiums covered by the company and many benefits paid at 100% for employees
  • Flexible, affordable gym memberships with 12,700+ options nationwide, including 24 Hour Fitness, EoS Fitness, Crunch Fitness, Anytime Fitness, Blink Fitness, Chuze Fitness, and more! No long-term contracts and FREE on-demand workout videos before you enroll
  • 401(k) retirement plan with a 50% company match on contributions up to 8%, supporting long-term financial security
  • Company wellness programs that support physical and mental well-being
  • Additional voluntary benefits and employee support resources
  • The opportunity to work alongside a highly talented team in an innovative, mission-driven environment

descriptionHtml:
About Maneva

Maneva is building the Thinking Factory: a factory floor that sees, understands, and acts on its own. Our Vision-to-Action AI turns video from off-the-shelf cameras into real-time decisions, with no rip-and-replace of existing infrastructure. We work with mid-market and enterprise manufacturers to deliver end-to-end outcomes, not dashboards:

  • Higher yields: catch defects and process drift as they happen, and cut scrap and downtime
  • Closed-loop integration: connect vision insights directly to MES, PLC, and other production systems so findings trigger action
  • Safer, compliant floors: detect safety and compliance risks continuously, instead of relying on periodic audits

Founded in 2022, Maneva raised a $27M Series A led by U.S. Venture Partners in June 2026 to push the frontier of our vision models, expand factory orchestration, and bring Thinking Factories to new industries and geographies. The models you build here will run on real production lines, where accuracy, latency, and reliability decide outcomes.

What You'll Do

  • Define the technical strategy and architecture for vision models across detection, VLM, and VLA workloads
  • Train, fine-tune, and adapt models (YOLO variants, open VLMs, VLA policies) on proprietary data, including distillation, quantization, and LoRA-style adaptation
  • Build data engines: labeling pipelines, auto-labeling with foundation models, active learning, and synthetic or simulated data
  • Design rigorous evaluation: benchmarks, regression suites, failure-mode analysis, and online metrics tied to product outcomes
  • Ship models to production under latency, memory, and cost limits, on cloud GPUs and edge hardware (TensorRT, ONNX, Jetson or similar)
  • Lead cross-team technical projects; write design docs; review code and models; mentor senior and mid-level engineers
  • Track the research frontier, decide what is worth adopting, and turn it into prototypes and product


Requirements

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years building and shipping ML systems, with focus on computer vision; BS/MS/PhD in CS, EE, or a related field, or equivalent experience
  • Deep hands-on experience with object detection and segmentation (YOLO family, DETR-style models), including training, tuning, and production deployment
  • Hands-on experience with VLMs (for example LLaVA-, Qwen-VL-, or PaliGemma-style models): fine-tuning, prompting, grounding, and evaluation
  • Experience with VLAs or embodied and robot-learning models (for example OpenVLA-, RT-2-, or pi0-style policies), or a clear record in adjacent multimodal work
  • Strong PyTorch skills and fluency with distributed training, mixed precision, and GPU profiling
  • Track record of taking models from research to production: model optimization, inference serving, monitoring, and iteration on real-world failures
  • Evidence of staff-level impact: setting direction across teams, making sound build-versus-adopt calls, and raising the bar for others
  • Clear written and verbal communication with engineers, researchers, and product leaders

Nice to have

  • Publications or open-source contributions in vision or multimodal learning
  • Experience with video understanding, 3D perception, or multi-sensor fusion
  • Experience with simulation, sim-to-real transfer, or reinforcement and imitation learning
  • Edge and embedded deployment experience (TensorRT, CUDA, quantization-aware training)
  • Experience with LLM tooling such as vLLM, or with RLHF-style post-training for multimodal models
  • This role may support work subject to U.S. export controls. Access to certain projects may require U.S.-person status (U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, refugee, or asylee) or export authorization


Benefits

Why Join Maneva?

  • Drive operational excellence in a fast-growing AI company transforming manufacturing through cutting-edge vision systems
  • Shape the future of project delivery by building scalable processes for AI system deployments
  • Work with world-class engineering talent while optimizing team performance and customer success
  • Gain exposure to cutting-edge Vision AI & IoT solutions across diverse manufacturing environments
  • Lead strategic initiatives that directly impact company growth and customer satisfaction
  • Build expertise in the rapidly expanding field of industrial AI and autonomous manufacturing

Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary based on location and experience - market rate
  • Equity participation in a high-growth AI startup
  • Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage
  • Flexible PTO and professional development opportunities
  • Remote-first culture with modern collaboration tools

We are committed to ensuring the security and privacy of all applicants. Please be aware that our company will never ask for sensitive personal information, via email, phone call or text message. We also do not require payment from applicants for any part of the hiring process.

If you are contacted by someone claiming to represent our company and asking for such information, please do not respond. Instead, report the incident to us immediately at IT-Security@Maneva.ai.

companyDescription:
New types of organization are needed to accelerate scientific progress.

Academic research groups and startup companies are essential to science and technology development. But there are some projects they just aren’t suited for. A university astronomy lab couldn’t have launched the Hubble Space Telescope on its own, nor would a venture-backed startup have built the Large Hadron Collider at CERN.

Hubble and CERN illustrate a common pattern in science: a need for projects that are bigger than an academic lab can undertake, more coordinated than a loose consortium or themed department, and not directly profitable enough to be a venture-backed startup or industrial R&D project.

Focused Research Organizations (FROs) are a new type of scientific institution designed to fill this gap.

descriptionHtml:
E11 Bio is on a mission to advance connectomics towards the scale of whole mammalian brains. We are a collaborative and interdisciplinary team of scientists and engineers engaged in a neuroscience moonshot project to develop a radical technology platform for scalable brain mapping. E11 Bio is a non-profit Convergent Research focused research organization located in Alameda, California, pursuing blue-skies neuroscience research yet operating like a nimble, tight-knit start-up. Read our technology roadmap .

We are seeking a creative and mission-driven Machine Learning Scientist to develop scalable automatic proofreading methods leveraging barcode and shape information. In this role, you will own core ML pipelines for automated proofreading of neuron and synaptic reconstructions in optical connectomics datasets, working closely with wet lab scientists, microscopists, and domain experts to ensure biological fidelity and scalability. Your work will directly support E11’s goal of making reliable connectomic data accessible to the broader neuroscience community.

In this role you will be focused on decreasing segmentation and proofreading costs for optical connectomics datasets that we are generating at E11, a critical bottleneck in the connectomics field. You will be responsible for improving initial segmentations using large spatial contexts with rich data features, and ingesting resulting datasets into scalable proofreading software for dissemination to the scientific community.

Responsibilities

  • Contribute to developing innovative ML approaches for automatic proofreading of segmentations in large PB-scale optical connectomics volumes, leveraging shape and barcode information
  • Own the deployment of scalable workflows to ingest large connectomic datasets into standard proofreading software (WebKnossos, CAVE)
  • Collaborate with academic and industry experts on building and extending tools for automated proofreading and interactive visualization
  • Develop, implement, and evaluate scalable pipelines for synapse detection and partner assignment in large-scale optical connectomics datasets, integrating morphological and protein labeling information
  • Identify and build ML-based image processing tools that remove key bottlenecks in our data processing and analysis pipeline
  • Maintain excellent laboratory science practices, communicate results through reports and presentations, and contribute to and assist in preparation of manuscripts, abstracts and other scientific documents.

Required Qualifications

  • Ph.D. in computer science, machine learning, applied math, computational biology or a related field in science and/or engineering or Ph.D.-equivalent publication history
  • 3-5 years of relevant work or research experience, with strong history of independent and autonomous execution of novel ML solutions
  • Strong background in computer vision and applying ML tools to the analysis of large microscopy data sets
  • Experience with software engineering best practices (e.g. version control, code reviews, etc)
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, record keeping ability, and attention to detail

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with graph, sequence, or point based ML methods (GNNs, Transformers, Pointnets, etc.)
  • Experience with processing large chunked data (e.g Zarr) in the cloud (e.g. AWS or GCP)
  • Experience with large scale connectomics data and tools (e.g. Neuroglancer, WebKnossos, CAVE, CATMAID, etc.)
  • Strong record of publications in peer reviewed scientific journals a plus.

In The First Six Months, You Will

  • Become familiar with our existing ML and distributed processing code bases
  • Own the processing (segmentations) of a new dataset end-to-end and identify areas for improvement (accuracy and efficiency)
  • Integrate internal graph-based methods for automatic proofreading into standard block-wise workflows for PB-scale optical connectomics volumes
  • Optimize ingestion of smaller segmentation graphs into standard proofreading software (e.g WebKnossos, CAVE) for improving efficiency of ground truth generation

In 12 Months, You Will

  • Develop novel innovative ML approaches for automatic proofreading of neuron segmentations, leveraging both shape and barcode information
  • Contribute to algorithmic development across the segmentation pipelines increasing computational throughput
  • Contribute to achieving cubic-mm scale reconstruction at 100x lower proofreading costs
  • Scale ingestion of PB-sized optical volumes into proofreading software and pilot proofreading and dissemination of large connectomic subgraphs

You would love this job if…

  • You are passionate about moonshot neuroscience, and want to broadly accelerate science through long-term commitment to a high-impact project with a tight-knit team
  • You have a strong desire and intrinsic motivation to work collaboratively and inclusively as part of an interdisciplinary team science effort
  • You are committed to the ethos of open science, and want to see your work transparently disseminated
  • You’re mission-driven, and are seeking an environment where you can take long-term risks on moonshot science, shielded from academic or for-profit incentives
  • You’re seeking a high-leverage, non-traditional opportunity to maximize the impact of your science, establishing relationships with key stakeholders in the neuroscience community

We Offer

  • An opportunity to help change the world and work with a world-class interdisciplinary team of scientists and engineers on a field-defining moonshot
  • Excellent medical, dental, and vision insurance through a PPO plan; parental leave.
  • Generous time off + paid holidays.
  • 401K matching up to 6% of base salary
  • Ample healthy and energizing food including daily lunches.
  • Stipend for fitness and wellness activities.

companySlogan: We’re securing America's food supply by building the AI farmer that automates our nation's farms 🍎
descriptionHtml:
At Orchard, we’re securing America’s food supply by building the AI Farmer that automates our nation’s farms. We are the industry leader, growing rapidly, and backed by more than $25 million from leading investors, including Quiet Capital, Shine Capital, and General Catalyst.

Every year, hundreds of billions of dollars in crop value are lost because critical farming decisions are made using incomplete and imprecise data. We’re building the technology to change that.

Our AI-powered camera systems mount to tractors and scan millions of trees, vines, and plants, capturing precise data on yield estimates, fruit size, crop health, disease, and more. We train edge vision AI models that analyze every plant and determine exactly what interventions and treatments it needs. That intelligence flows into FruitScope OS, our farm-management platform, where growers can understand their crops, make better decisions, and direct operations in the field.

Today, Orchard’s technology is trusted by some of our nation’s largest farms. They use our products to grow higher-quality crops while reducing chemical use and operating costs, helping them farm more profitably and sustainably than ever before.

Our Culture

  • Unshakeable Resilience – Our customers feed millions of people, and our customers depend on us. We are ultra-hardworking, never give up, and we do whatever it takes.
  • Always Keep Moving – We move fast, waste no time, and have an extreme bias towards action. Progress compounds every day, and our impact is measured in decades.
  • Improve Everything – At 1% success, we save millions of pounds of food from going to waste. If we are 100% successful we will impact the lives of billions of people across the world.
  • Farmers First – Every team member spends at least a few days in the fields with our farmers each month.
  • No Job Beneath Us – We’re low ego, own every outcome, and are all working towards the same goal.

The Role

In order to analyze billions of fruit on farms all year long, our advanced, tractor-mounted camera systems have to know a.) precisely where they are, and b.) everything about the fruit they are seeing. In addition, all of this happens fast, on compute running on the edge, in complex, real-world environments where our systems are subject to all sorts of conditions.

We are looking for a Robotics Software Engineer to invent creative, practical, and robust solutions to real-world computer vision problems relating to perception and localization.

About The Role
