descriptionHtml:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an AI Engineer based remotely in the United States.

As an AI Engineer, you will help shape the next generation of intelligent manufacturing systems by developing advanced computer vision and multimodal AI models. You will define technical architecture and lead the development of models capable of interpreting real-time factory environments and translating visual insights into operational decisions. Working across detection, vision-language models, and vision-language-action systems, you will take solutions from research and experimentation to production deployment. You will also build scalable data pipelines, evaluation frameworks, and optimized inference systems for both cloud and edge environments. Collaborating with engineering, research, and product teams, you will influence technical direction and mentor other engineers. Your work will directly improve manufacturing quality, efficiency, safety, and automation.

Accountabilities

You will lead the technical development and deployment of advanced AI models, ensuring they deliver reliable performance in real-world industrial environments. Your responsibilities will include:

  • Define technical strategy and architecture for computer vision models, including detection, vision-language models (VLMs), and vision-language-action (VLA) workloads.
  • Train, fine-tune, and adapt models such as YOLO variants, open-source VLMs, and VLA policies using proprietary datasets.
  • Apply model optimization techniques, including knowledge distillation, quantization, and LoRA-based adaptation.
  • Build and improve data engines, including labeling pipelines, foundation-model-assisted auto-labeling, active learning, and synthetic or simulated data generation.
  • Design rigorous evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, regression test suites, and failure-mode analyses to measure model performance.
  • Establish online metrics connected to real product and operational outcomes.
  • Deploy models into production environments while meeting latency, memory, and cost constraints across cloud GPUs and edge hardware.
  • Optimize inference and deployment using technologies such as TensorRT, ONNX, NVIDIA Jetson, or comparable platforms.
  • Lead cross-functional technical initiatives, prepare architecture and design documentation, review code and models, and mentor senior and mid-level engineers.
  • Monitor advances in AI research, assess emerging technologies, and translate relevant developments into prototypes and production-ready capabilities.

Requirements

The ideal candidate combines deep hands-on machine learning expertise with the technical leadership required to guide complex AI initiatives from research through production. You should have a strong background in computer vision and multimodal learning, along with experience building reliable systems at scale. Key qualifications include:

  • 5+ years of experience building and deploying machine learning systems, particularly in computer vision.
  • Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Extensive hands-on experience with object detection and segmentation models, including YOLO-family and DETR-style architectures.
  • Practical experience training, tuning, and deploying computer vision models in production environments.
  • Experience working with vision-language models such as LLaVA, Qwen-VL, or PaliGemma, including fine-tuning, prompting, grounding, and evaluation.
  • Experience with vision-language-action models, embodied AI, or robot-learning systems such as OpenVLA, RT-2, or pi0, or a strong track record in adjacent multimodal AI fields.
  • Advanced proficiency in PyTorch and familiarity with distributed training, mixed-precision techniques, and GPU profiling.
  • Proven ability to take models from research to production, including optimization, inference serving, monitoring, and continuous improvement based on real-world performance.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership, including setting direction across teams, making informed build-versus-adopt decisions, and raising engineering standards.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with engineers, researchers, and product leaders.

Nice To Have

  • Research publications or open-source contributions in computer vision or multimodal learning.
  • Experience with video understanding, 3D perception, or multi-sensor fusion.
  • Familiarity with simulation, sim-to-real transfer, reinforcement learning, or imitation learning.
  • Experience deploying models on edge and embedded devices, including TensorRT, CUDA, and quantization-aware training.
  • Knowledge of LLM infrastructure and tooling such as vLLM.
  • Experience with RLHF-style post-training techniques for multimodal models.

Benefits

  • Market-competitive salary based on experience and location.
  • Equity participation in a high-growth AI company.
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance.
  • Flexible paid time off.
  • Professional development opportunities.
  • Remote-first working environment supported by modern collaboration tools.
  • Opportunity to work with experienced engineering talent on advanced Vision AI and IoT solutions.
  • Exposure to diverse manufacturing environments and real-world industrial AI applications.
  • Opportunity to lead strategic technical initiatives and contribute directly to product and business growth.

How Jobgether Works

We use an AI-powered matching process to ensure your application is reviewed quickly, objectively, and fairly against the role's core requirements. Our system identifies the top-fitting candidates, and this shortlist is then shared directly with the hiring company. The final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.

We appreciate your interest and wish you the best!

descriptionHtml:
About The Company

At Torc, we have always believed that autonomous vehicle technology will transform how we travel, move freight, and do business. A leader in autonomous driving since 2007, Torc has spent over a decade commercializing our solutions with experienced partners. Now a part of the Daimler family, we are focused solely on developing software for automated trucks to transform how the world moves freight. Join us and catapult your career with the company that helped pioneer autonomous technology, and the first AV software company with the vision to partner directly with a truck manufacturer.

Meet the Team

Torc is marching towards its AV 3.0 strategy. The Scene Generation team builds sensor simulation based on Neural Rendering and generative models for Torc's data-driven simulator. High-quality data from novel scenarios closes the domain data gap, solving one of the biggest challenges for safe autonomous driving. The team works on state-of-the-art approaches for Neural Rendering and data generation for camera, LiDAR, and Radar sensor data, contributing to Torc's data workflow for training and validation across the complete AV stack. As Staff ML Engineer, you will lead this team, setting its technical direction and day-to-day priorities.

What You'll Do


  • Serve as the team's technical lead, owning key design decisions and driving consensus across engineers and stakeholders.
  • Set and own the technical vision and roadmap for the Scene Generation team's Neural Rendering and generative modeling work, aligned to Torc's AV 3.0 strategy.
  • Lead the Scene Generation team day to day, prioritizing work, unblocking engineers, and making the final call on architecture and technical approach.
  • Implement and guide the team in applying the latest research advances in Neural Rendering and generative models.
  • Translate cutting edge research into production quality Camera, LiDAR, and Radar sensor simulation that scales perception simulation and AV 3.0 training.
  • Own the neural rendering framework end to end, from research, design, and implementation through testing, cloud integration, and deployment.
  • Understand the integration of the framework in a cloud environment and automate the pipeline to scale target verification and validation of our autonomous trucks.
  • Design, implement, test, and deploy shippable production quality software using disciplined software development processes, setting the technical bar for the team.
  • Work within the cloud machine learning ecosystem alongside other machine learning services across the company, owning integration and scaling decisions for the team's pipeline.
  • Proactively assess current capabilities to identify areas for improvement, proposing and driving solutions that align with core strategy and operations.
  • Drive alignment across team interfaces to the rest of the organization, representing Scene Generation's roadmap, priorities, and constraints to peer teams and leadership.
  • Mentor, coach, and grow engineers on the team, and play an active role in hiring, onboarding, and career development for the group.


What You'll Need To Succeed


  • Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering or related technical field plus demonstrates competences and technical proficiencies typically acquired through 10+ years of experience OR Master’s Degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering or related technical field plus demonstrates competences and technical proficiencies typically acquired through 7+ years of experience OR PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering or related technical field plus demonstrates competences and technical proficiencies typically acquired through 5+ years of experience.
  • Proficiency in Python and deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch.
  • PhD or equivalent work experience of 8+ years in a relevant field (CS, Robotics, Electrical Engineering), with industry experience shipping production software and leading technical teams.
  • Proven expertise in Neural Rendering (Neural Radiance Fields and 3D Gaussian Splatting) and generative models (Diffusion Models, Flow Matching).
  • Experience with production data in the context of robotics and/or autonomous driving
  • Background in Computer Vision, Computer Graphics, 3D Reconstruction, or 3D Computer Vision.
  • Experience handling autonomous driving sensor data across multiple timestamps and sensor modalities, including cameras, LiDAR, and radar.
  • Recognized as an expert in the discipline, conducting complex, high impact work under minimal supervision and with wide latitude for independent judgment.
  • Experience with VDI and cloud-based machine learning development environments.
  • Demonstrated experience leading a team or serving as a technical lead, setting direction and driving consensus across engineers and stakeholders.
  • Track record of mentoring and developing engineers, including more senior individual contributors.

companySlogan: Intercepting tomorrow's threats, today.
descriptionHtml:
America is critically deficient in production of defensive munitions- we currently produce shipborne interceptors in the few hundreds per year while our adversaries are producing offensive threats in the tens of thousands per year. Furientis was started to help solve this problem- introducing a new class of cost-effective, high production rate, interceptor missiles. We're seeking motivated individuals who internalize this problem and are eager to apply their past experience in similar industries (aerospace, defense, automotive/racing, robotics) and out of the box thinking to solve this problem for the US and its allies.

About The Team

The Seeker Team builds the eyes and the targeting logic of our weapon system: a low-cost, mass-producible, multimodal missile seeker that leans on commercial supply chains where they outperform, and vertically integrates wherever possible. On a modern missile, the seeker is 40 to 60% of unit cost and often drives overly long delivery cycles; accordingly, the seeker team is at the tip of the spear for delivering capability to our customers and value to the taxpayer.

Seeker design has exactly two real constraints: physics and mission. Nothing else is a show-stopper, only an obstacle to overcome. We are a small, deeply technical team that drives capability through ingenuity and bias for action and ships hardware that flies. This is a wear-many-hats environment where you must be comfortable "building the airplane in flight" and stepping well outside your comfort zone; a narrowly scoped role with clean handoffs is not what this team offers.

This is an AI-native team. Through fluent use of cutting-edge agentic coding tools, one engineer here consistently out-delivers a much larger conventional team. You will have opinions about where these tools help and where they do not, provide governance input, and build out an AI-centric workflow from day one.

About The Role

You will contribute to the production of perception and estimation algorithms at the core of our seeker: detection, tracking, classification, and aimpoint localization on infrared (IR) imagery and fused sensor measurements, against targets that fight back. As part of the Seeker Team, you will research, implement, optimize, and validate algorithms in these areas, including modern AI and machine learning (ML) methods where they earn their place. Runtime efficiency is a hard constraint: everything you build must run within a strict latency budget on embedded flight-compute hardware. You will work closely with the broader Seeker Team to carry your algorithms from first prototype into flight.

What You'll Do

  • Design and implement object detection algorithms for mid-wave infrared (MWIR) and long-wave infrared (LWIR) imagery, robust to clutter, domain shift, and countermeasures.
  • Develop multi-object tracking and state estimation: filtering, data association, and line-of-sight estimates for missile guidance.
  • Implement track lifecycle management: initialization, maintenance, confirmation, and termination under real sensor conditions.
  • Develop segmentation, classification, and discrimination algorithms that separate targets from decoys, debris, and background.
  • Develop aimpoint localization and the associated image-processing methods that support terminal accuracy.
  • Contribute to perception-related sensor fusion, combining IR and X-band radar measurements into a consistent track picture.
  • Implement, optimize, and validate your algorithms for real-time flight: measured latency, covariance and confidence you can defend, and performance proven in simulation, in hardware-in-the-loop testing, and in flight data.
  • Research and prototype advanced AI and ML methods within perception and estimation, and help mature the ones that prove out into the flight pipeline.


Skills We're Hiring For

  • Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in Optical Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Applied Math, Physics, or a related field; Master of Science (M.S.) or Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) preferred.
  • 5 to 7 years of experience in applied computer vision, perception, or estimation on real sensor data.
  • Fluency in state estimation: the Kalman filter family, including nonlinear variants and interacting multiple model (IMM) approaches, applied with judgment.
  • Data association at multi-target scale: joint probabilistic data association (JPDA), multiple hypothesis tracking, or modern equivalents, chosen with judgment.
  • Classical optical image and signal processing as a working toolkit, with emphasis on methods for optical sensors: spatial and temporal filtering, morphology, non-uniformity and fixed-pattern noise handling, and techniques for imagery with a low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
  • Statistical rigor as a habit: normalized estimation error squared (NEES) and normalized innovation squared (NIS) consistency testing, covariance validation, and calibrated confidence.
  • 3+ years of experience using python to create, alter, and maintain libraries of algorithms within a modern Git & CI/CD framework.


Bonus Points For

  • Rust for real-time implementation and familiarity with embedded CUDA
  • Missile, interceptor, or guided-munition perception or tracking experience.
  • Track-before-detect or other methods for detection and tracking at low SNR.
  • IR or other non-visible-band sensor experience, including synthetic-to-real domain adaptation.
  • TensorRT or comparable edge inference deployment experience.
  • Multi-sensor registration, boresight exploitation, or radar measurement familiarity.
  • Modern machine learning fluency (PyTorch or equivalent): training, evaluating, and shrinking perception models with measured accuracy tradeoffs.
  • Daily use of agentic coding tools (Claude Code or similar) to multiply your output.


Eligibility & Logistics Location: On-site at our Los Angeles, CA HQ; remote work is not available. Monthly weekend travel for test events and supplier engagements. Clearance: A clearance is not required for this position. Must be a U.S. Person.

Equal Opportunity & Export Compliance Furientis is an equal-opportunity employer. To comply with U.S. export control laws, employment is contingent on eligibility to access export-controlled information.

descriptionHtml:
About Atomic

Atomic is a venture studio and venture capital firm that builds and scales companies from the ground up. We partner with exceptional founders to launch transformative businesses across industries including AI, fintech, healthcare, consumer, enterprise software, and more. We've launched and scaled more than 20 companies including Hims & Hers, Exowatt, Replicant, Found, Golden Child, Sauron, and Homebound.


Who We Are

Sauron, one of Atomic's newly incubated companies, is the home security company of the future. Homeowners today lack compelling options when it comes to peace of mind against vulnerabilities, and total command and control of their home; there is no definitive, protective brand in the space. Leveraging cutting-edge AI, sensor technology, and nonlethal deterrence, Sauron brings next-generation technology to homeowners to protect their families and property. Incubated by the serial entrepreneur Kevin Hartz and Atomic, Sauron has raised an $18M seed round from leading venture capital firms and angel investors, including 8VC and Flock Safety CEO Garret Langley, to build the new perception system for the home.


The Role - Senior Perception Engineer


Perception is the foundation of the Sauron product. Every decision the system makes (what to show a homeowner, what to disregard, what to escalate) depends on whether we have correctly understood what took place outside the home. We are seeking the person who will own this domain.


Our hardware operates around the home and must complete its mission reliably in all environmental conditions: at night, in adverse weather, and in the presence of occlusion and deliberate evasion. In this role, you will set the technical direction for how we achieve that, including what we sense, what we infer, which problems are best addressed through models and which through systems, and what "ready to ship" means in measurable terms rather than impressions.


You will own the perception architecture and the accuracy, latency, and cost tradeoffs that underpin it. You will work closely with the hardware team to define sensing requirements across successive product generations, and you will serve as the authority that cloud, product, and hardware teams consult to understand what perception can and cannot do. You will write a substantial amount of code, focused on the most difficult problems, but your success will be measured by whether the perception system as a whole becomes better, faster, and more trustworthy.


We Value...

  • Collaboration, pair programming, and teamwork.
  • Taking ownership across the stack.
  • Test-driven development, and refactoring regularly to keep our codebases healthy.


You Will Contribute By...

  • Evolving the pipeline architecture so cameras can come and go, and configuration can change, without disrupting live video or losing object identity.
  • Setting the boundary between systems and models. You decide what belongs in the compiled service, what belongs in the inference graph, and where the performance ceiling really is.
  • Owning perception quality end to end. Defining what good looks like in numbers: evaluation data, a regression harness, and a defensible story on model choice for our hardware.
  • Extracting the maximum value from our sensors. Fusing every observation available while staying robust to occlusion, poor lighting, and deliberate evasion.
  • Taking the service from "runs" to "trustworthy unattended." Failure detection, graceful degradation, and observability good enough that we know why something broke without a site visit.
  • Closing the loop from the field. Using deployment data to find headroom, and building the dataset and evaluation infrastructure that makes that repeatable.
  • Leading the work and the people. Setting direction across perception, reviewing the hard changes, and owning the interfaces perception exposes to the rest of the product.


Your Background Includes...

  • Around 5+ years building production systems, with several at staff scope: owning a system's architecture, not just its tickets.
  • Significant professional experience with perception or machine learning for hardware products in a safety-critical field - aerospace, robotics, medical devices, autonomous vehicles, or physical security.
  • Deep modern C++. This is a C++20 codebase with Abseil, gRPC, and CMake; you should be comfortable owning lifetime, threading, and shutdown semantics in a long-running daemon.
  • Real GStreamer or media-pipeline experience, DeepStream or another NVIDIA video stack: pads, probes, caps negotiation, bus messages, and the specific pathology of a pipeline that is alive but not moving.
  • Applied computer vision you have shipped - multi-object tracking, re-identification, or multi-camera association - and the judgment to know when the answer is a better model versus better geometry versus better plumbing.
  • A clear grasp of linear algebra, optimization, statistics, and algorithms, and the theory behind the techniques you reach for.
  • Experience across the deep-learning lifecycle: PyTorch or an equivalent framework, custom layers and operations, optimizing networks for inference on edge compute, reproducibility, and honest evaluation.
  • GPU inference in practice: TensorRT engines, batching, fp16, and reasoning about where latency actually goes.
  • Edge instincts. You have debugged something that only fails on the device, after nine hours, on one customer's network, and you treat observability and failure classification as part of the feature.
  • Python fluency. A meaningful share of the load-bearing logic is Python, and you will be the one deciding what it costs us.
  • A generalist mindset - able to dive in wherever the bottleneck is, from cloud training infrastructure down to embedded systems.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to set technical direction and disagree productively with adjacent teams.


Nice to Have

  • NVIDIA Jetson in production - JetPack, L4T, Yocto images, or the joy of cross-building for aarch64.
  • Previous experience building multi-camera tracking systems.
  • Video surveillance, VMS, or ONVIF/RTSP integrations, and knowing how cameras actually misbehave.
  • GPU architecture and CUDA programming.
  • Familiarity with VLMs and other multi-modal models for semantic scene understanding.
  • Owning model evaluation: datasets, metrics, and the discipline to reject a model that benchmarks better but ships worse.

- Evolving the pipeline architecture so cameras can come and go, and configuration can change, without disrupting live video or losing object identity.
- Setting the boundary between systems and models. You decide what belongs in the compiled service, what belongs in the inference graph, and where the performance ceiling really is.
- Owning perception quality end to end. Defining what good looks like in numbers: evaluation data, a regression harness, and a defensible story on model choice for our hardware.
- Extracting the maximum value from our sensors. Fusing every observation available while staying robust to occlusion, poor lighting, and deliberate evasion.
- Taking the service from "runs" to "trustworthy unattended." Failure detection, graceful degradation, and observability good enough that we know why something broke without a site visit.
- Closing the loop from the field. Using deployment data to find headroom, and building the dataset and evaluation infrastructure that makes that repeatable.

Job Description

Senior or Staff Machine Learning Scientist

Cleveland Clinic is seeking a Senior or Staff AI Scientist to develop and translate advanced AI solutions across surgery, perioperative care, clinical research, and healthcare operations.

Embedded within the Department of Plastic Surgery and InSITE Research Group, this individual will work directly with surgeons, clinicians, and investigators while collaborating with enterprise AI, engineering, analytics, cloud, and MLOps teams. The role offers a distinctive opportunity to develop AI for the operating room and perioperative environment using surgical video, medical imaging, physiologic signals, sensor data, robotics, electronic health record data, and patient-reported outcomes.

We are seeking a scientist with deep expertise in computer vision, video understanding, or multimodal machine learning, complemented by experience in at least one adjacent area such as generative AI, robotics, predictive modeling, or clinical natural language processing. The successful candidate will contribute across data engineering, model development, rigorous evaluation, clinical validation, and production deployment, helping move high-value projects from clinical need to scalable implementation.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and validate machine learning models for surgical, perioperative, clinical, and operational applications.
  • Advance computer vision, multimodal learning, generative AI, predictive modeling, and real-time clinical decision support.
  • Develop machine learning systems using time-synchronized surgical video, medical imaging, physiologic waveforms, device and sensor streams, robotic telemetry, longitudinal electronic health record data, and patient-reported outcomes.
  • Create methods to recognize surgical phases, anatomy, instruments, events, workflow, and the evolving state of the operating room.
  • Build and extend reusable technical infrastructure for surgical intelligence, including multimodal data ingestion and synchronization, data quality controls, annotation and labeling workflows, dataset versioning, reproducible training pipelines, model evaluation, prospective validation, deployment, and post-deployment monitoring.
  • Explore physical AI applications that connect perception, prediction, and action through intelligent surgical systems, robotics, sensor-enabled environments, and human-machine collaboration.
  • Collaborate on emerging approaches such as world models, vision-language-action models, and reinforcement learning for surgical and perioperative environments.
  • Develop AI solutions addressing surgical safety, quality, patient-reported outcomes, operations, documentation, and perioperative efficiency.
  • Translate clinical and operational needs into technically rigorous projects with clear data requirements, validation strategies, and measures of success.
  • Provide technical leadership across multidisciplinary projects by shaping system architecture, establishing evaluation standards, reviewing technical work, and coordinating clinicians, researchers, data engineers, ML engineers, enterprise platform teams, and external collaborators from early development through implementation.
  • Contribute to peer-reviewed publications, presentations, grants, and collaborative research.
  • Apply responsible and human-centered AI practices throughout development and clinical translation, including privacy-preserving data use, bias and subgroup evaluation, interpretability appropriate to the use case, uncertainty communication, human-factors assessment, documentation, and clearly defined human oversight.

Required Qualifications

  • PhD in computer science, engineering, data science, biomedical informatics, robotics, applied mathematics, statistics, or a related quantitative field.
  • Advanced knowledge of machine learning and deep learning, with demonstrated depth in at least one relevant technical area and the ability to select appropriate methods, design rigorous experiments, diagnose failure modes, and evaluate whether model performance is sufficient for the intended clinical or operational use.
  • Strong proficiency in Python and demonstrated ability to develop maintainable, tested machine learning software using modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or JAX; experience with relevant model and data ecosystems, including Hugging Face where appropriate.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and validating machine learning models using complex real-world data.
  • Ability to communicate effectively and collaborate with clinicians, researchers, engineers, and operational leaders.
  • Strong record of independent technical problem-solving and multidisciplinary teamwork.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with surgical video, medical imaging, physiologic signals, sensor fusion, robotic systems, electronic health record data, or patient-reported outcomes.
  • Experience developing models for real-time or safety-sensitive environments.
  • Experience with temporal modeling, surgical phase recognition, or human-machine interaction.
  • Experience with cloud AI platforms, Databricks, scalable data pipelines, or distributed computing.
  • Experience with MLOps, including model deployment, monitoring, reproducibility, and lifecycle management.
  • Experience translating AI research into clinical, operational, or other real-world environments.
  • Familiarity with responsible AI, privacy, security, data governance, and validation in regulated settings.
  • Strong publication, applied research, or AI product development record.
  • Experience coordinating engineers, data scientists, or external technical collaborators.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is an accomplished AI scientist who wants to work closely with surgeons and clinical teams on consequential healthcare problems. This individual will bring recognized expertise in a core technical discipline while remaining versatile enough to contribute across modeling, multimodal data infrastructure, validation, deployment, and research.

The successful candidate will be intellectually curious, collaborative, and comfortable working in the operating room and perioperative environment. They will understand that meaningful surgical AI requires more than model performance. It requires clinical immersion, thoughtful integration of multiple data streams, prospective validation, responsible implementation, and effective human-machine interaction.

Why Join Us

  • Develop AI directly within the operating room and perioperative environment.
  • Advance computer vision, multimodal AI, physical AI, surgical intelligence, and personalized decision support
  • Build intelligent systems integrating surgical video, imaging, physiologic, sensor, robotic, and clinical data.
  • Shape emerging applications of robotics, embodied intelligence, and human-machine collaboration in surgery.
  • Develop AI across the continuum from research concept to clinical or operational implementation.
  • Build platforms that can extend across projects, procedures, and specialties.
  • Collaborate with leading clinical, research, enterprise AI, engineering, and external technology teams.
  • Combine publication-quality research with meaningful clinical impact.

Cleveland Clinic is committed to using AI to improve patient outcomes, personalize care, reduce administrative burden, and increase healthcare efficiency. Our AI culture emphasizes technical excellence, curiosity, collaboration, responsible innovation, and measurable clinical impact.

About Us

Cleveland Clinic's vision is to become the best place for care and the best place to work in healthcare. We are committed to providing a safe, stable, and financially fulfilling work environment. Cleveland Clinic is ambitiously investing in growth. Being a physician-led organization means doing what is best for the patients, every day.

Cleveland Clinic is one of the world's largest and busiest health centers. Patients come to Cleveland Clinic from all over the world. We offer advanced treatment for all illnesses and disorders of the body.

Cleveland Clinic is a nonprofit, multispecialty academic medical center that's recognized in the U.S. and throughout the world for its expertise and care. Cleveland Clinic integrates clinical and hospital care with research and education. Located in Cleveland, Ohio, it was founded in 1921 by four renowned physicians with a vision of providing outstanding patient care based upon the principles of cooperation, compassion and innovation. Cleveland Clinic has pioneered many medical breakthroughs, including coronary artery bypass surgery and the first face transplant in the United States. Among Cleveland Clinic's 80,642 employees worldwide are more than 5,743 salaried physicians and researchers, and 20,166 registered nurses and advanced practice providers, representing 140 medical specialties and subspecialties. Cleveland Clinic is a 6,690-bed health system that includes a 173-acre main campus near downtown Cleveland, 23 hospitals, more than 270 outpatient facilities, including locations in northeast Ohio; southeast Florida; Las Vegas, Nevada; Toronto, Canada; Abu Dhabi, UAE; and London, England. In 2025, there were 15.9 million total outpatient visits, 343,000 hospital admissions and observations, and 336,000 surgical cases throughout Cleveland Clinic's health system. Patients came for treatment from every state and 185 countries.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Principal Machine Learning Engineer, Vision AI based in the United States.

In this principal-level engineering role, you will shape the architecture and development of a next-generation Vision AI platform designed to transform how restaurants operate. You will lead the creation of secure, reliable video infrastructure and intelligent services that turn visual data into actionable insights for business operators. Combining deep distributed systems expertise with hands-on machine learning engineering, you will own technical direction while continuing to design, code, prototype, and ship production solutions. You will integrate advanced computer vision and vision-language models, build robust inference and monitoring systems, and bring new AI-powered capabilities to customers. Working in a fast-moving, collaborative environment, you will mentor engineers, establish technical standards, and help define how AI-assisted development accelerates product innovation.

Accountabilities

  • Architect and build the core Vision AI platform, including video capture, ingestion, storage, processing, and delivery infrastructure, ensuring security, reliability, and scalability.
  • Develop and own backend services that process video footage, run computer vision models, and convert visual information into actionable observations, metrics, and insights.
  • Select, integrate, and optimize vision models, including vision-language models, while building the supporting machine learning infrastructure.
  • Design and maintain production inference pipelines, model evaluation frameworks, and monitoring systems to track model performance and reliability.
  • Collaborate with machine learning engineers to integrate and mature models for deployment in real-world customer environments.
  • Develop and deliver customer-facing Vision AI features across multiple product experiences and platforms.
  • Define the technical architecture and long-term direction of the Vision AI platform, balancing current product needs with future development opportunities.
  • Remain highly hands-on, writing production code, prototyping ideas, testing solutions, and delivering working products.
  • Partner with engineering, product, and other cross-functional teams to manage integrations, dependencies, and technical decisions.
  • Incorporate AI coding assistants and agent-based development tools into everyday engineering workflows, helping establish practices that improve development speed and quality.
  • Mentor engineers and establish high standards for software quality, security, privacy, reliability, and maintainability.
  • Build reusable platform capabilities that make future Vision AI use cases easier and more efficient to develop.

Requirements

  • At least 10 years of software engineering experience, including designing and delivering distributed systems and data pipelines in production environments at scale.
  • Strong expertise in backend engineering and cloud infrastructure, preferably AWS.
  • Experience with event-driven architectures and messaging systems such as Apache Pulsar or Kafka.
  • Proficiency in Kotlin, Java, or comparable programming languages, along with practical experience using Python.
  • Strong understanding of machine learning systems, including model training, tuning, serving, and production operations.
  • Experience building and operating production ML systems, including inference pipelines, model evaluation, and performance monitoring.
  • Familiarity with video technologies, including video streams, codecs, and tools such as FFmpeg.
  • Proven ability to make pragmatic architectural decisions, building solutions appropriate to current needs while allowing room for future growth.
  • Experience taking ambiguous concepts from early prototypes through production deployment and real customer adoption.
  • Strong hands-on engineering capabilities and a genuine interest in writing and shipping production code.
  • Regular use of AI-assisted development tools and agent harnesses, such as Claude Code or Cursor.
  • Experience building applications or services using large language model or vision-language model APIs.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to align engineering and product stakeholders around technical decisions and clearly explain architectural trade-offs.
  • Comfort working in an evolving environment where priorities, processes, and technical approaches may change as new customer needs emerge.
  • Ability to experiment, learn quickly, and focus on practical solutions that address real operational challenges.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience developing computer vision, video analytics, or camera-based products.
  • Familiarity with real-time video pipelines and streaming technologies such as Amazon Kinesis Video Streams, GStreamer, or WebRTC.
  • Experience managing connected device fleets, including device provisioning, authentication, remote updates, and constrained network environments.
  • Experience building privacy-sensitive systems that process video or personal data.
  • Background in restaurant, retail, hospitality, drive-through, or other operationally complex industries.

Benefits

  • Competitive annual base salary based on geographic pay zone:
    • Zone A: $230,000–$368,000 USD.
    • Zone B: $200,000–$320,000 USD.
    • Zone C: $180,000–$288,000 USD.
  • Additional compensation opportunities, which may include bonuses or other cash compensation depending on eligibility.
  • Equity compensation.
  • Comprehensive benefits and total rewards designed to support employees' health, financial well-being, and changing needs.
  • Remote work arrangement within the United States.
  • Access to AI-powered tools and resources across engineering and other business functions.
  • Opportunities to shape emerging AI products and influence platform architecture.
  • A collaborative and inclusive working environment that encourages experimentation, learning, and professional growth.

Our system identifies the top-fitting candidates, and this shortlist is then shared directly with the hiring company. The final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.

We appreciate your interest and wish you the best!

Why Apply Through Jobgether?

This processing is based on legitimate interest and pre-contractual measures under applicable data protection laws (including GDPR). You may exercise your rights (access, rectification, erasure, objection) at any time.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. Job Summary

The C++ Engineer (Computer Vision/Embedded Systems) will help build and maintain a cross-platform computer vision stack used in embedded and Android/Linux environments. In this roll you will work on performance-sensitive code, building systems, testing infrastructure, and developing tooling in a containerized workflow.

descriptionHtml:
Perception Targeting Engineer - Build the Sensing and Targeting Software That Tells a Space-Based Laser Where to Look

Remote (U.S.)

Opportunity Summary

Join a newly funded space and defense startup building the first spacecraft to carry a high-energy laser into orbit. As a Perception Targeting Engineer, you will turn camera, LiDAR, and radar data into an accurate picture of the space around the spacecraft, then write the targeting and control logic that puts the laser where it needs to go.

This role spans space domain awareness, sensor fusion, autonomous path planning, and targeting control laws. Very few people have done targeting work in space, so we want engineers who have built real-time perception and targeting on the ground, in the air, or underwater and are ready to take it to orbit. This is a fully remote role open to candidates anywhere in the U.S.

About Us

We are a stealth-stage space and defense company building the first spacecraft to put a high-energy laser in orbit. Hundreds of billions of dollars in satellites operate today with no way to defend themselves, and we are building the capability to protect them. Our three founders have designed, built, and launched complex space hardware at leading space companies and defense primes. Backed by an oversubscribed seed round from tier-one venture investors, we are building our demonstration spacecraft over the next 12 months.

Job Duties

  • Build perception pipelines that detect, track, and characterize objects in orbit from onboard cameras and other sensors.
  • Fuse camera, LiDAR, and radar data into reliable target state estimates for space domain awareness.
  • Develop targeting algorithms and control laws that select aimpoints and command the pointing system.
  • Create autonomous path planning that positions the spacecraft relative to targets.
  • Deploy and optimize vision and AI models on embedded AI compute hardware for real-time operation.
  • Model engagements and sensor performance in STK and custom simulation tools.
  • Calibrate sensors and own timing, alignment, and latency budgets across the targeting loop.
  • Work closely with GNC, flight software, and optics engineers to close the loop from sensing to pointing.
  • Validate algorithms through simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, and ground demonstrations.
  • Write production code in C++ and Python.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field.
  • 4+ years building perception, tracking, or targeting systems deployed on real hardware.
  • Hands-on experience with object detection, multi-object tracking, and sensor fusion.
  • Experience writing control laws or closed-loop tracking that act on perception outputs.
  • Proficiency in C++ and Python, plus OpenCV, PyTorch, or similar libraries.
  • Experience bringing up models on embedded GPUs or AI accelerators, including unfamiliar hardware.
  • Comfort owning work end to end on small teams, from algorithm to running hardware.
  • U.S. citizen or permanent resident, willing to obtain a security clearance.

Preferred Experience

  • Targeting, fire control, or acquisition, tracking, and pointing for directed energy or air defense systems.
  • Space domain awareness, rendezvous and proximity operations, or optical navigation.
  • Perception and autonomy for eVTOL aircraft, drones, ground vehicles, or underwater vehicles.
  • Targeted image processing, LiDAR, or radar signal processing.
  • STK modeling and analysis.
  • Master's or PhD in Computer Vision, Robotics, or a related field.

Why Join Us

  • Pioneer targeting for the first high-energy laser to operate in space.
  • Fully remote role.
  • No-cost medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees, with subsidized family coverage.
  • Meaningful early-stage equity.
  • Work alongside founders who have designed, built, and launched complex space hardware.
  • Relocation support if company locations evolve as we grow.

Compensation Details

$180,000 - $250,000 + equity

Position Summary

We are seeking a motivated Data Scientist to research, develop, and enhance AI/ML algorithms for computer vision and healthcare applications. This role involves developing and improving deep learning models, maintaining high standards of data quality, optimizing models for efficient deployment, and translating advances in AI research into practical healthcare solutions. The Data Scientist will collaborate with clinical partners and internal stakeholders to understand clinical and business needs and develop appropriate technical solutions. The ideal candidate will be capable of independently managing research and development projects while contributing effectively within cross-functional teams. Success in this role requires strong technical and communication skills, attention to detail, persistence, and a commitment to staying current with advances in AI/ML and computer vision.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

  • Research, develop, evaluate, and enhance machine learning and deep learning algorithms for computer vision applications, translating advances in AI research into practical healthcare solutions.
  • Implement and optimize model deployment pipelines to enable efficient, scalable, and hardware-optimized inference.
  • Apply model optimization techniques to improve computational efficiency and inference performance while maintaining model accuracy.
  • Maintain data quality and integrity throughout the data lifecycle to support robust algorithm development, training, and evaluation.
  • Collaborate with clinical partners and internal stakeholders to understand clinical and business needs and translate them into appropriate AI/ML solutions.
  • Independently manage assigned research and development projects from problem formulation through implementation, evaluation, and delivery.
  • Ensure reproducibility of analyses and experiments through clear documentation, version-controlled workflows, and effective knowledge sharing.
  • Stay current with advances in AI/ML, computer vision, and related technologies and evaluate their applicability to ongoing research and development.
  • Communicate technical methods, results, and recommendations effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Qualifications

  • M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.
  • Minimum of two years of relevant research or professional experience in computer vision. For candidates with a master’s degree, the required experience must be professional experience obtained after completion of the degree.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

  • Strong programming skills in Python and experience developing maintainable, reproducible code for machine learning applications.
  • Strong foundation in state-of-the-art deep learning architectures (e.g., vision transformers) for computer vision tasks including image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation.
  • Proficiency with deep learning frameworks and libraries, including PyTorch and TensorFlow.
  • Strong understanding of AI/ML evaluation metrics, benchmarking methodologies, and best practices for rigorous computer vision model validation.
  • Solid understanding of model optimization techniques, including pruning, quantization, mixed-precision inference, and other strategies for improving computational efficiency and inference performance.
  • Working knowledge of model deployment and inference tools, such as ONNX, LibTorch, and TensorRT.
  • Self-driven and capable of independently navigating ambiguous research problems, working with incomplete data, and delivering high-quality results.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare technical documentation, reports, and scientific manuscripts.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working with multispectral and/or hyperspectral imaging data.
  • Experience with generative AI models for medical image synthesis and simulation.
  • Experience applying AI/ML methodologies to healthcare or biomedical applications, with demonstrated contributions to successful research, clinical, or product outcomes.

Physical Requirements

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.

Travel

N/A

descriptionHtml:
Job Description

Role and Responsibilities

We are seeking a talented Software Engineer – Color, RIP and Imaging to develop next-generation image processing algorithms, color management pipelines, and visual computing software. The role combines color science and software engineering to improve image quality, color accuracy, and real-time visual performance across software and hardware platforms.

Key Responsibilities

  • Algorithm Development: Design, implement, and optimize algorithms for color transformation, transparency, image processing, machine learning, and AI.
  • Pipeline Integration: Develop and maintain end-to-end image processing and color management pipelines using technologies such as ICC profiles and OpenCV.
  • Collaboration: Work closely with hardware, video, UI, engineering, QA, and marketing teams to deliver complete solutions.
  • Performance Optimization: Develop high-performance, low-latency C/C++ or CUDA/OpenCL code for imaging pipelines running on CPU, GPU, or dedicated hardware.
  • Testing & Calibration: Develop automated test suites, spectral measurement setups, and image quality metrics such as PSNR and Delta E to validate visual quality.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Color Science, Imaging Science, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field.
  • Experience: 0–3 years of professional experience in digital image processing, computer vision, or graphics.
  • Programming: Strong proficiency in C++ and Python, with hands-on experience in OpenCV, SciPy, or similar image processing libraries.
  • Domain Knowledge: Understanding of color spaces, colorimetry, gamma correction, and rendering pipelines.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced Degree: Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Applied Mathematics, Color Science, Imaging Science, Computer Science, or Electrical Engineering. Candidates should complete their degree by January 2027.
  • GPU Programming: Experience with CUDA, HLSL/GLSL, or Metal.
  • Machine Learning: Familiarity with deep learning for image enhancement, super-resolution, or neural ISP using PyTorch or TensorFlow.

Desirable but not mandatory:

  • Printing domain experience is a plus.
  • Ability to work effectively in a matrix environment.
  • Comfortable working with ambiguity.

What’s in it for you?

  • Opportunity to work in a multinational product organization.
  • Learn from experienced professionals and leaders.
  • Exposure to the latest technology and tools.
  • Accelerated career growth.
  • Flexible and hybrid work environment with a healthy work-life balance.
  • Culture of meritocracy, inclusion, empowerment, and fun.
  • Competitive pay and benefits.

Compensation

The salary range is USD $120,000–$135,000. Actual compensation will depend on experience, skills, and geographic location.

descriptionHtml:
This is a hands-on modeling role. You will design, train, and evaluate the deep learning models that turn large microscopy volumes into usable data: segmentation, the stitching and alignment of image tiles and sections, and the detection and classification models that follow. The job will heavily depend on expertise and fluency in DL frameworks like PyTorch: reading the literature, choosing an architecture that fits the data, training it at scale, and finding out where and why it fails.

You report to the Head of Computation, and work, as needed, with other Mindspan teams (Microscopy and Optics, Expansion Microscopy, Scalable Chemistry, and Automation and Industrialization), using logic and evidence to advance your work so as to boost the performance of all.

The position is intended for a generalist: someone who is as comfortable adapting a pretrained vision model as writing a new loss function, and who picks the model to fit the problem rather than the reverse. Given the multidisciplinary nature of the job, it is ideal for a person who enjoys problem solving across intellectual boundaries, at the level of concepts as well as of hands-on debugging. It also requires systematic documentation, analysis, and iterative problem solving, to arrive at working models, apply them, and share them.

  • Design, train, and evaluate deep learning models for volumetric microscopy data, including dense segmentation, boundary and affinity prediction, and object detection.
  • Build models and methods that stitch and align image tiles and serial sections into consistent volumes.
  • Adapt pretrained and foundation vision models to our imaging modalities, and decide when a new architecture is worth the cost.
  • Run controlled experiments: ablations, held-out evaluation, and error analysis that shows which failure modes a change fixed and which it introduced.
  • Work with the pipeline and annotation teams to move models into production, and to request the ground truth that the next model needs.
  • Documentation and training: keep experiment records that others can reproduce, with the reasoning behind each design choice.

The disorders of the brain affect over 1,000,000,000 people around the world: Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s, stroke, and other conditions. We operate with a sense of urgency, even as we look to understand the brain at its most fundamental levels.

We are hypercollaborative, and focused on impact over short-term markers of productivity. Creativity and failure are the stepping stones to scale, and working together with “strong opinions, weakly held” is our style.

We solve real engineering problems the best way we can: inventing fast when we have to, and using good existing solutions where they exist. We believe hard problems only yield to many disciplines working together, so collaboration is required, not optional.

We expect people to explore the unknown, which means making mistakes daily, owning them, and learning from them to improve and excel.

We are recruiting a team of scientists and engineers who exemplify all these values.

Required Qualifications.

  • Advanced degree or equivalent industry experience in computer science, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, physics, computational biology or neuroscience, or a related field.
  • Direct hands-on experience designing and training deep learning models.
  • Demonstrated experience with image segmentation or dense prediction on 3D or large 2D image data.
  • Strong software engineering: Python, version control, testing, and code that other people can run and extend.
  • Experience training on multi-GPU systems or a compute cluster.
  • Excellent engineering judgment and scientific rigor, including the discipline to tell a real improvement from noise.

Preferred Qualifications.

  • Experience with image registration, stitching, or alignment of large tiled or serial-section datasets.
  • Experience with connectomics or other biological microscopy data (electron, light, or expansion microscopy).
  • Experience with self-supervised learning, or with adapting large pretrained vision models to a new domain.
  • Experience with chunked array formats (Zarr, N5, precomputed) and data too large for one machine.
  • Publications, open-source models, or results on public benchmarks.

The ideal candidate is a scientist-engineer who can read a paper on Monday and have a working reimplementation by Friday. You are intellectually curious, relentlessly practical, and happiest when solving problems that have never been solved before. You choose methods by what the data needs, and you can explain why a model works as well as why one fails.

You have a strong detail orientation and exceptional organizational, planning, interpersonal, and communication skills. You are good at writing, can work independently and lead and manage, and can prioritize and multitask as needed. Self-motivation, commitment to high quality standards, and a service-oriented mindset are all key. You have good judgment, balancing flexibility and focus, action and planning, speed and thoughtfulness, as appropriate. You are open to giving and receiving feedback, constructively and thoughtfully, to advance scientific missions and personal growth.

This is an in-person job. Flexible hours may be required at times.

The chance to build the core models of a new research institute alongside some of the most adventurous scientists in the field, with real autonomy and a direct line to the people setting the scientific agenda. You will get to contribute to addressing one of the most important unmet medical needs of our time, as part of the initial team. You will learn lots of things that probably cannot be learned any other way, as you solve problems, build, and work with others. As Mindspan grows, we expect this role to grow with it. We are excited to invest in someone who wants to take on increasing responsibility over time.

Comprehensive health, dental, vision, and family benefits, and a matching retirement contribution.

Competitive salary ($180,000 to $260,000), depending on experience.

descriptionHtml:
About Rivian

Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.

As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.

Role Summary

Failsafe is a foundational pillar of the Autonomy safety architecture. In this Staff ML Software Engineer role, you will play a key part in driving and delivering high-quality, real-time onboard models and algorithms to evaluate sensor reliability, scene hazards, and perception capabilities. You will design, train, and ship production-grade solutions that enable our vehicles to understand environmental limitations, sensor degradations, and safety boundaries in 3D.

As an experienced technical expert, you will own the end-to-end lifecycle of the failsafe system: defining safety metrics, engineering diagnostic algorithms, benchmarking on-vehicle performance, and establishing tight feedback loops. A key focus of this role is dedicated to multi-modal scene understanding, ensuring the vehicle can gracefully handle degraded states (such as lens blockage, adverse weather, or road surface hazards) to trigger automated sensor recoverability routines or minimum risk maneuvers.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the design, delivery and deployment of production-grade, highly reliable failsafe algorithms for L3 and L4 platforms, focusing on real-time sensor blockage, degradation, and occlusion detection.
  • Develop multi-modal (camera and/or LiDAR) models to analyze real-time road conditions, including surface wetness, friction/mu-estimation, and physical drivability hazards.
  • Design intelligent algorithms to trigger automated sensor-cleaning hardware and recovery strategies, directly maximizing ADAS uptime in challenging environments
  • Architect systems to evaluate and report real-time 3D perception uncertainty and capability limits, interfacing directly with downstream planning and central safety fallback managers.
  • Partner closely with cross-functional teams to define strict safety boundaries, establish rigorous testing benchmarks, and guide system-level architecture trade-offs.

Qualifications

  • BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or a highly related quantitative field.
  • 7+ years of professional experience scaling production-grade MLsoftware for autonomy or robotics.
  • Proven track record of hands-on experience building algorithms for autonomous vehicle perception or environmental scene understanding.
  • Solid understanding of modern perception pipelines and data representation across multiple modalities (cameras, LiDAR, and Radar).
  • Strong proficiency in C++ and Python alongside experience with real-time software performance optimization and latency profiling.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive complex technical roadmaps and deliver components in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience designing failsafe, fail-operable, or degraded-state software architectures for safety-critical systems.
  • Hands-on experience with sensor degradation modeling (such as camera soil, lens glare, rain, or LiDAR spray) and system-level ODD degradation modeling.
  • Deep understanding of onboard edge deployment and managing cloud telemetry loops to monitor model performance in the field.
  • Experience collaborating directly with systems safety teams to translate hazard analysis and risk assessments into robust software implementations.

Pay Disclosure

We are a multi-disciplinary team of engineers, scientists, and management professionals dedicated to developing and commercializing AI/ML/Software solutions that address our customers’ most significant challenges and opportunities.

Most important to us are our culture and values. Etegent’s culture embodies respect, authenticity, collaboration, flexibility, curiosity, and fun.


The Position:

Etegent is seeking Machine Learning Engineers (MLEs) to work with our Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) group based in the Beavercreek office. MLEs will work in a team environment with Etegent teammates, customers, and other researchers from leading academic institutions, government organizations and commercial entities.


We deliver solutions in the domains of AI/ML, data science, software, and visualization to address geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) challenges for Department of Defense and Intelligence Community (DoD/IC) customers. We develop data science tools to analyze large, diverse datasets from a variety of sensor types (SAR, ISAR, GMTI, HIS, EO, IR). We design and implement algorithms to perform pattern recognition, such as statistical and deep learning techniques, to identify meaningful trends and patterns. We wrap these algorithms in accessible, scalable software to be deployed on customer systems, often requiring containerized software and custom user interfaces for visualization.


This position is based in Beavercreek, OH with the expectation of being in Etegent’s office or at a customer facility 5 days a week.


The Candidate:

More so than seeking a candidate with specific training and experience, Etegent is seeking a candidate with an innate curiosity and passion for learning and understanding, tempered by a recognition of the pragmatic constraints inherent in developing real solutions to real problems. Etegent needs an MLE who is flexible and adaptable, having the desire and ability to learn new skills and develop new capabilities to take on challenges outside their current realm of experience. We are seeking very sharp, curious, well-rounded, adaptable people who can learn and grow as required to confront the challenges at hand.


Job Responsibilities:

  • Effectively communicate status updates, and other important information, with the team and group leader.
  • Execute research-and-development tasks in close collaboration with the team and group leader according to a set project schedule.
  • Gives effective feedback to others; contributes to the writing of project updates and final reports.
  • Understand, design, and implement algorithms for signature exploitation. This includes traditional feature extraction and state-of-the-art deep learning approaches.
  • Implement efficient signal/image processing techniques including radar signal processing, electro-optical and infrared image processing.
  • Develop and deploy data science tools for ingestion, visualization, and analysis of large, diverse data sources.
  • Implement machine learning, data mining and statistical algorithms for pattern recognition and anomaly detection.
  • Provide expertise in data analytics and algorithm development for diverse data sources and applications.
  • Apply statistical techniques to evaluate algorithm performance.
  • Coordinate with teammates and users to instantiate research concepts in efficient, modular, and well-documented software.


Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in the fields of Computer Science, Engineering, Physics, Applied Math, or Statistics.
  • Previous signal processing, computer vision, or machine learning experience.
  • Experience developing ML models using standard ML frameworks (PyTorch, Tensorflow, or similar).
  • Experience developing software tools capable of deriving value from large, diverse datasets.
  • Background in data science, statistics, and/or computer vision.
  • Experience creating python-based user interfaces for data visualization.
  • Experience with Python, Git, and Linux.
  • An active TS security clearance.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with remote sensing data products such as SAR, ISAR, EO, GMTI, HSI, and OPIR.
  • Experience creating user interfaces with Dash, Streamlit, or other similar frameworks.
  • Familiarity with DoD/IC customers.
  • Experience maintaining successful relationships and developing business with R&D customers.
  • History of technical presentations and publications in relevant fields.


Attributes:

  • Independent and innovative thinker with an ability to work in an autonomous environment.
  • Demonstrates curiosity with a focus on innovating solutions for tasks.
  • Effective communicator who can collaborate with teammates and customers to solve problems.
  • Able to take personal ownership and responsibility over their work.


Working at Etegent:

At Etegent, you'll be a part of a fast-growing organization that combines a small-company feel with big-company resources and opportunities. We know that work-life balance is incredibly important, which is why in addition to your competitive salary, medical/dental/vision plan, and a generous annual company 401(k) contribution, you'll enjoy the following:

  • Flexibility: Not a morning person? No problem. We only ask that you begin your day by 10:00am. Also, you will enjoy a flexible schedule and some ability to telecommute.
  • Casual Dress: We know that incredible things can be achieved by people in casual clothing. We allow employees to dress in the way that is the most comfortable to them.
  • Professional Development: Continuous learning on us. Reimbursement provided for up to 100% of qualifying education expenses.
  • Food: Keep your energy levels up with our well-supplied snack and beverage kitchen and enjoy a weekly lunch with your talented colleagues on Free Lunch Thursdays.
  • Fun employee events: Enjoy frequent employee get-togethers outside of work!


Competitive compensation based on qualifications and experience of candidate.

descriptionHtml:
Laza Medical, a Shifamed Portfolio Company, is at the forefront of developing state-of-the-art imaging solutions for cardiovascular applications. Our mission is to democratize top-quality cardiovascular imaging using robotics and AI. We recently raised up to $160 million in Series B structured financing. GE HealthCare led the round, with participation from returning investors Unorthodox Ventures, PA MedTech, and AMED. The financing will support our mission to transform the cardiac catheterization laboratory through intelligent imaging technology. To learn more about Laza Medical, please visit https://lazamedical.com/.


ABOUT SHIFAMED

Founded in 2009 by serial entrepreneur Amr Salahieh, Shifamed LLC is a privately held medical technology incubator focused on the development of novel medical products to address clinical needs in the rapidly evolving fields of cardiology and ophthalmology.


Description:


As a Software Engineer focusing on Medical Visualization and software integration you will engineer the intelligence behind a revolutionary robotic platform with ultrasound imaging and AI for interventional cardiology. You will work at the challenging intersection where software meets physics, integrating the real-time medical imaging visualization and imaging algorithm from prototypes to production. This is not just about writing code; it is about owning critical subsystems of a life-saving device. You will drive technical decisions, build high-fidelity simulations, and deliver production-grade software that translates complex algorithms into clinical reality.


Responsibilities, Skills & Hands-On Experience:

  • Analyze requirements, design, and implement software for image guided robotics.
  • Design, implement, and integrate 3D visualization features using ImFusion suite.
  • Develop and execute comprehensive software testing frameworks, leveraging debugging tools for issue identification and resolution.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to design and implement automation systems within an FDA-compliant Quality Management System (QMS).
  • Evaluate new and emerging designs, technologies, and components.


Preferred Skills & Hands-On Experience:

  • Experience developing software under FDA Quality System Regulations and IEC 62304 processes for Class II or Class III medical devices.
  • Familiarity with Linux development and system maintenance.
  • Familiarity with software testing frameworks and debugging tools.


Education & Work Experience:

  • BS, MS Degree in Computer Science or equivalent experience in a related field
  • Minimum of 2 years of relevant experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to systematically troubleshoot and debug complex systems.
  • Proficiency in C++, Python, C++.
  • Experience with agile software development life cycles including design, implementation, deployment, and maintenance for production grade systems.
  • High levels of independence and technical ownership.
  • Experiences with SQA and software release and deployment process.
  • Experience porting modern C++ applications.
  • Experience with 3D Graphics is a plus
  • Experience with ImFusion suite is a strong plus.


Our salary ranges are calculated by role, level, and location. Please note that your position within that range will be determined by your job-related knowledge, location, skills, experience, relevant education, and training/certifications. The base salary range for this full-time position is between $100,000 - $130,000 + equity + benefits.

descriptionHtml:

CFD Research has earned multiple national awards for successful application and commercialization of innovative component/system technology prototypes, multi-physics simulation software, multi-disciplinary analyses, and expert support services. Based in Huntsville, Alabama where laboratory facilities and headquarters are located, CFD Research also has office and laboratory facilities in Dayton, Ohio, prototyping test and evaluation facilities in Hollywood, Alabama, and office facilities in Fort Walton Beach, Florida. CFD Research is an ISO9001:AS9100D registered company and is appraised at CMMI Level II for Services. CFD Research is a 100% ESOP (employee-owned company) recognized in Inc. Magazine's Inc5000 as a top growing company for four of the last five years. Learn more at www.cfd-research.com

CFD is seeking a Remote Sensing Software Engineer, to develop advanced SDA and remote sensing exploitation pipelines, guide technical direction, and work with multi-disciplinary teams building high-fidelity space observation analytics. This work will shape next‑generation tools that integrate imaging physics, ML-based behavior inference, and multi‑sensor fusion.

  • Architect end‑to‑end remote sensing processing systems for EO/IR missions
  • Develop radiometric and spectral response models
  • Support development of advanced imaging algorithms including multi-frame super-resolution, deconvolution, target phenomenology detection, and low-SNR enhancement
  • Implement ML‑based anomaly detection, behavior classification, and object discrimination frameworks
  • Design multi-sensor fusion pipelines integrating GEOINT, Radar, RF, and EO/IR data using Bayesian or ML-based methods
  • Conduct trajectory estimation and 3D kinematic modeling, including IOD, parallax exploitation, and uncertainty quantification
  • Architect scalable scientific computing solutions using Python, C++, CUDA, HPC clusters, or cloud-native platforms

Basic Qualifications

  • Candidate must possess an ACTIVE TOP SECRET with SCI ELIGIBILITY clearance to be considered.
  • 3-8+ years of experience in remote sensing, image/signal processing, or GEOINT data exploitation
  • Experience with satellite characterization, orbital regimes, Domain-specific applications or SDA operational workflows
  • Experience with Python or other Object-oriented programming languages such as C++ or JavaScript
  • Understanding of enterprise software development best practices, to include version control, interfacing with HPC/cloud computing, containerization, unit testing, Linux-based systems, and AGILE development
  • Experience with ML systems for imagery processing, target detection, tracking, or object classification
  • Bachelor’s degree in related STEM field
  • U.S. Citizenship is REQUIRED.

Desired Qualifications

  • Experience with remote sensing systems in support of missile warning/tracking missions
  • Experience with building/training synthetic models for simulation‑aided training
  • Experience integrating EO/IR, RF, Radar, or GEOINT tracks into fused solutions
  • Record of publications, whitepapers, presentations or mission briefings
  • Experience with uncertainty quantification, Kalman filtering, or tracking algorithms
  • Experience with AI‑augmented development workflows or agentic tools
  • Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Software Engineering or related field
  • TS/SCI clearance is PREFERRED; TS/SCI with CI polygraph IS AN ADDED PLUS.

Location: This role is based in the Dayton, OH area, and is 100% onsite.

Benefits: CFD Research offers competitive salaries and excellent employee benefits, including an employer matching 401(k) and Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP). CFD Research offers our Full-Time, permanent employee-owners a highly competitive insurance package, including medical, vision, and dental insurance. Additionally, we offer company paid leave, compensation time, parental leave, long-term and short-term disability, accidental death and dismemberment, and life insurance. Part-Time and Temporary employee-owners may receive partial or reduced benefits and leave time based on their employment status level. Performance appraisals occur twice a year and annual pay increases are based upon corporate goals, personal development, performance, and outstanding achievements. In addition, group and individual bonuses are awarded for exceptional performance.
